[package]
name = "test-fuzz"
version = "0.0.0"
publish = false
edition = "2021"

[package.metadata]
cargo-fuzz = true

[dependencies]
libfuzzer-sys = "0.4.9"
stylus-sdk = "=0.9.0"
alloy-primitives = { version = "=0.8.20", default-features = false }

[dependencies.openzeppelin-crypto]
path = "../lib/crypto"

# fuzz targets

[[bin]]
name = "merkle"
path = "fuzz_targets/merkle.rs"
test = false
doc = false
bench = false

[[bin]]
name = "keccak"
path = "fuzz_targets/keccak.rs"
test = false
doc = false
bench = false

# corpus generators

# name must be in format 'gen-{{fuzz-target}}-corpus
[[bin]]
name = "gen-merkle-corpus"
path = "src/merkle/corpus.rs"
test = false
doc = false
bench = false

build
modules
node_modules
package-lock.json
package.json
--- .config / .cargo ---
.cargo:
config.toml

.config:
nextest.toml
[target.wasm32-unknown-unknown]
rustflags = [
    "-C",
    "link-arg=-zstack-size=8192",
    "-C",
    "target-cpu=mvp",
    "-C",
    "target-feature=+bulk-memory",
]

[target.aarch64-apple-darwin]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-undefined", "-C", "link-arg=dynamic_lookup"]

[target.x86_64-apple-darwin]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-undefined", "-C", "link-arg=dynamic_lookup"]
[profile.ci.junit]
path = "junit.xml"
--- clippy.toml / rustfmt.toml ---
doc-valid-idents = ["OpenZeppelin", ".."]
max_width = 80
format_macro_matchers = true
group_imports = "StdExternalCrate"
imports_granularity = "Crate"
reorder_impl_items = true
use_field_init_shorthand = true
use_small_heuristics = "Max"
wrap_comments = true

===== scripts/bench.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
set -e

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR"
cd ..

# Optimize contract's wasm binary by crate name.
opt_wasm() {
  local CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME=$1
  local CONTRACT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}.wasm"
  local CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}_opt.wasm"

  echo
  echo "Optimizing $CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME WASM binary"
  # https://rustwasm.github.io/book/reference/code-size.html#use-the-wasm-opt-tool
  wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 -o ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME" ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_BIN_NAME"
}

# Retrieve all alphanumeric contract's crate names in `./examples` directory.
get_example_crate_names() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2038
  # NOTE: optimistically relying on the 'name = ' string at Cargo.toml file
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs grep 'name = ' | grep -oE '".*"' | tr -d "'\""
}

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  -Z build-std=std,panic_abort \
  -Z build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort

# Optimize contract's wasm for gas usage.
for CRATE_NAME in $(get_example_crate_names); do
  opt_wasm "$CRATE_NAME"
done

export RPC_URL=http://localhost:8547
export DEPLOYER_ADDRESS=0xcEcba2F1DC234f70Dd89F2041029807F8D03A990

# No need to compile benchmarks with `--release`
# since this only runs the benchmarking code and the contracts have already been compiled with `--release`.
cargo run -p benches
echo "This benchmarks measure gas execution cost,
 the 21000 EVM base gas fee is omitted."
echo
echo "To measure non cached contract's gas usage correctly,
 benchmarks should run on a clean instance of the nitro test node."
echo
echo "Finished running benches!"

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Function to retrieve all Cargo.toml paths in the ./examples directory
get_example_dirs() {
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs -n1 dirname | sort
}

  local CRATE_PATH=$1

  echo

  cd "$CRATE_PATH"

  cargo stylus export-abi

  echo

  echo "Done!"

  echo

  cd "$ROOT_DIR"
}


for CRATE_PATH in $(get_example_dirs); do
  check_abi "$CRATE_PATH"
done

#!/bin/bash
set -e

mydir=$(dirname "$0")
cd "$mydir" || exit
cd ..

# Check contract wasm binary by crate name
check_wasm() {
  local CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME=$1
  local CONTRACT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}.wasm"

  echo
  echo "Checking contract $CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME"
  cargo stylus check -e https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc --wasm-file ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_BIN_NAME"
}

# Retrieve all alphanumeric contract's crate names in `./examples` directory.
get_example_crate_names() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2038
  # NOTE: optimistically relying on the 'name = ' string at Cargo.toml file
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs grep -m 1 'name = ' | grep -oE '".*"' | tr -d "'\""
}

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  -Z build-std=std,panic_abort \
  -Z build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort

for CRATE_NAME in $(get_example_crate_names); do
  check_wasm "$CRATE_NAME"
  sleep 2
done

===== scripts/nitro-testnode.sh =====
#!/bin/bash

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR" || exit

HAS_INIT=false
HAS_DETACH=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
  -i | --init)
    HAS_INIT=true
    shift
    ;;
  -d | --detach)
    HAS_DETACH=true
    shift
    ;;
  -q | --quit)
    NITRO_CONTAINERS=$(docker container ls -q --filter name=nitro-testnode)

    if [ -z "$NITRO_CONTAINERS" ]; then
      echo "No nitro-testnode containers running"
    else
      docker container stop $NITRO_CONTAINERS || exit
    fi

    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "OPTIONS:"
    echo "-i|--init:         clone repo and init nitro test node"
    echo "-d|--detach:       setup nitro test node in detached mode"
    echo "-q|--quit:         shutdown nitro test node docker containers"
    exit 0
    ;;
  esac
done

TEST_NODE_DIR="$MYDIR/../nitro-testnode"
if [ ! -d "$TEST_NODE_DIR" ]; then
  HAS_INIT=true
fi

if $HAS_INIT; then
  cd "$MYDIR" || exit
  cd ..

  git clone -b release --recurse-submodules https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro-testnode.git
  cd ./nitro-testnode || exit
  git checkout c7a58620c431266c90f9d422eca6627e24586e60 || exit

  ./test-node.bash --no-run --init || exit
fi

cd "$TEST_NODE_DIR" || exit
if $HAS_DETACH; then
  ./test-node.bash --detach
else
  ./test-node.bash
fi

     278 CHANGELOG.md
# Changelog

These crates follow [semver](https://semver.org).

## [0.10.10](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.10) - 2026-10-02

### New

- Detect when Stylus activations are paused on the target chain and report a clear `ActivationsPaused` error instead of a generic activation failure [#458](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/458)

### Fixed

- Support `ruint >=1.17.1` and drop the vulnerable exact pin [#457](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/457)

## [0.10.9](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.9) - 2026-08-11

### New

- Add opt-in reproducible `wasm-opt` (Binaryen) optimization: a `[wasm-opt]` table in `Stylus.toml` pins a Binaryen version and flags, applied identically during deploy and verification and folded into the project hash [#449](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/449)

## [0.10.8](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.8) - 2026-07-06

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus verify` for fragmented (large) contracts whose init code is split across multiple deployment transactions [#445](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/445)

## [0.10.7](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.7) - 2026-05-19

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus verify` not forwarding `--endpoint` and `--skip-clean` flags to inner Docker invocation

## [0.10.6](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.6) - 2026-05-15

### New

- Add Dockerfile for building `cargo-stylus-base` Docker image from the monorepo
- Add reproducible Docker build path to `cargo stylus deploy` — previously deploy always built locally even when `--no-verify` was omitted, making Docker verification unreliable on cross-platform setups

### Fixed

- Fix reproducible Docker builds for workspace projects: mount workspace root instead of CWD so workspace-level `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and path dependencies are available inside the container
- Fix `cargo stylus verify` not forwarding `--contract` flag to inner Docker invocation, causing incorrect contract selection in multi-contract workspaces
- Fix reproducible build failing when base Docker image exists locally but not on Docker Hub

## [0.10.5](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.5) - 2026-04-16

### Changed

- Deprecate `reentrant` feature flag and `deny_reentrant` entrypoint guard — reentrancy safety is provided by automatic storage cache flushing in high-level call functions, making the guard redundant
- Rewrite reentrancy documentation to center cache flushing as the primary safety mechanism

## [0.10.4](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.4) - 2026-04-09

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus new` panic when installed from crates.io registry [#421](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/421)

## [0.10.3](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.3) - 2026-04-01

### New

- Detect ABI selector collisions at compile time within `#[public]` blocks [#401](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/401)

### Fixed

- Fix `sol_interface!` ABI decode panic on multi-value return types containing dynamic types (e.g. `returns (string, uint256)`) [#414](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/414)
- Fix `cargo stylus new` leaving projects in a broken state when dependency resolution fails [#416](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/416)
- Fix codehash-keepalive command sending read-only call instead of transaction [#411](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/411)

### Changed

- Update Rust toolchain to 1.91.0 and alloy dependencies to latest (alloy-primitives/alloy-sol-types 1.5.7, alloy 1.7.3) [#410](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/410)
- Update MSRV to 1.91.0 [#410](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/410)
- Remove exact version pins on `ruint`, `branches`, and `rclite`; disable `ruint` default features to prevent `std` leaking into WASM builds [#413](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/413)
- Switch ABI decoding to validating variants that reject malformed data [#415](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/415)
- Adopt stricter `rustfmt` configuration [#417](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/417)
- Extensive integration test improvements for examples [#365](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/365)
- Improve smoke test for `cargo stylus new` with scaffolding verification [#416](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/416)

## [0.10.2](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.2) - 2026-03-09

### Fixed

- Pin `keccak` dependency to `>=0.1.6` to avoid resolving to broken `0.1.5` [#397](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/397)
- Fix subcrate READMEs to point to repo root instead of broken symlinks [#398](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/398)
- Fix docs compilation error [#394](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/394)
- Fix 404 links and editorial nits [#376](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/376)

## [0.10.1](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.1) - 2026-03-09

### New

- Support for deploying large contracts via fragmented deployment, including constructor support for fragments [#383](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/383)
- Add `--wasm-file` flag to deployment CLI for deploying pre-built WASM files [#389](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/389)

### Changed

- Add AssemblyScript SDK to README [#386](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/386)

## [0.10.0](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.0)

### New

- Introduction of a new library for building and deploying stylus contracts: `stylus-tools`
- Support for cargo workspaces. Cargo-stylus now supports building and deploying contracts within a cargo workspace. Contracts are marked with a `Stylus.toml` file. Future configuration will be added to this file to facilitate per-contract and workspace-wide configuration options for contracts.
- Addition of a new `contract-client-gen` feature flag which allows contracts within a crate to be used as a "library" to be called by other contracts.
- Support for nested structs in return types
- More convenient integer functions for storage
- Support for custom storage slots
- Support for tuples in return types
- cargo stylus codehash-keepalive command

### Changed

- Update calls / deploys / logs to use noew hostio model
- Additional integration tests
- Upgrade alloy version
- More example contracts from Stylus By Example
- Use alloy::Bytes type instead of our own
- Improvements to CI
- Move `cargo-stylus` into the `OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs` repo to simplify development and release of new cargo-stylus versions
- Updates to `cargo stylus new` for creating workspaces and individual contracts (`--workspace` and `--contract` flags respectively)
- Allow pure functions in trait-based inheritance model
- Traits used for contract routing inheritance must now use the `#[public]` macro
- Mini-alloc has been moved to its own crate since it has been stable for some time

### Fixed

- Fix panic when using `alloy_primitives::utils::keccak256()`
- Proper encoding of tuples containing dynamic length types
- Add missing definitions in `export-abi` output
- Support for associated types in `export-abi`
- Disallow shadowing of constructor function selector
- Better sanitization of names in `export-abi` output
- Disallow `AbiType` definitions which shadow solidity reserved type names
- Fix panic when using `console!` macro in testing environment
- Allow parameterized traits with associated types
- Increase size of `ConstString` used to define potentially long `AbiTypes
- Support for solidity mapping types in `sol_storage!` macro

### Removed

- Removal of deprecateed code from previous versions
- Old inheritance model no longer supproted

## [0.9.2](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.9.2) - 2025-09-23

### Fixed

- Fix segfault when testing with the keccak function in alloy.

## [0.9.0](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.9.0) - 2025-05-20

### Changed

- Fix formatting by @amsanghi in #222
- Add Stylus constructors by @gligneul in #184
- first pass implementation of trait based inheritance by @rory-ocl in #223
- Fix Cargo Stylus Replay by @gligneul in #225
- Update CHANGELOG.md (main) by @gligneul in #228
- Remove mark_used function to reduce binary size by @gligneul in #235
- Port 0.8.3 changes to main by @gligneul in #231
- add StorageU96 int alias by @0xNeshi in #234
- Remove the HostIO-caching feature by @gligneul in #237
- Add a README to Stylus Test by @rauljordan in #239
- Be more strict with special function names by @gligneul in #242
- Resolve Audit Feedback Related to TestVM and Fallbacks by @rauljordan in #241

## [0.8.3](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.8.3) - 2025-03-18

### Fixed

- Fix stylus SDK dependencies in wasm32
- Do not require contract crate to define stylus-test feature

## [0.8.2](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.8.2) - 2025-03-11

### Fixed

- Fix cargo stylus replay [#226](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/226)

## [0.8.1](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.8.1) - 2025-02-21

### Fixed

- Add Reentrant Feature to Stylus Test When Enabled in SDK [#221](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/221)

## [0.8.0](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.8.0) - 2025-02-12

### Added

- Define a Host Trait for the Stylus SDK [#199](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/199)
- Define Initial WasmHost Implementation for Wasm Targets [#200](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/200)
- Use a Boxed, Dyn Host Trait for Contract Initialization [#203](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/203)
- Define Testing VM to Implement the Mock Trait [#204](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/204)
- Rename Stylus-Host to Stylus-Core and Make Calls Part of the VM [#206](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/206)
- Make Deployment Logic Part of the Host Trait [#207](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/207)
- Add unit tests to storage bytes [#213](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/213)
- Add Missing Methods to Host Trait [#210](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/210)

#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

export RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"

# Print version information
rustc -Vv
cargo -V

# We have to use cargo metadata because we can't exclude a feature directly in cargo test.
# See: https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/3126
FEATURES=$(cargo metadata --format-version=1 --no-deps | jq -r '.packages[] | .features | keys | join("\n")')
FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | grep . | sort | uniq | grep -v default) # cleanup

# Remove export-abi, this feature is tested in the integration tests CI job.
FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | grep -v export-abi)

# Remove integration-test because it runs in another CI job.
FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | grep -v integration-tests)

# Remove trybuild tests on nightly because they depend on the compiler output.
FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | grep -v trybuild)

# Remove contract-client-gen feature.
# This feature is tested individually since it considerably change the structure of the output code.
FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | grep -v contract-client-gen)

FEATURES=$(echo "$FEATURES" | tr ' ' ',')

test() {
    local features="$1"
    echo "Testing with features: $features"
    local targets="$2"

    cargo check --locked -F "$features" --workspace
    cargo test --no-default-features $targets -F "$features" --workspace
}

test "$FEATURES" ""
# disables doctests when testing contract-client-gen
cargo check -F contract-client-gen --workspace

# Run trybuild tests separately without other features
if [[ "${CFG_RELEASE_CHANNEL-}" != "nightly"* ]]; then
    cargo test -p stylus-proc -F trybuild-tests
fi
----- ci/clippy.sh
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $0 [option]"
  echo ""
  echo "Options:"
  echo "  -c, --contract-client-gen                 Run clippy on stylus-proc with contract-client-gen feature"
  echo "  -e, --export-abi                          Run clippy on stylus-proc with export-abi feature"
  echo "  -a, --all-excluding-special-features      Run clippy excluding contract-client-gen and export-abi features"
  echo "  -h, --help                                Display this help message"
}

run_all_clippy() {
  echo "Running clippy on all packages excluding contract-client-gen and export-abi features..."

  # Get all crates in the workspace
  workspace_members=$(cargo metadata --format-version=1 | jq -r '.workspace_members[] | split(" ")[0]')

  # For each crate, run clippy with all features except contract-client-gen
  for crate in $workspace_members; do
    if [[ "$crate" == *"erc20"* || "$crate" == *"erc721"* ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    # Get features for this crate excluding the ones we don't want
    features=$(cargo metadata --format-version=1 \
      | jq -r ".packages[] | select(.id == \"$crate\") | .features | keys[] |
              select(. != \"contract-client-gen\" and . != \"export-abi\")" \
      | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')

    echo "Running clippy on $crate with features: $features"
    if [ -n "$features" ]; then
      cargo clippy -p "$crate" --all-targets --no-default-features --features "$features" -- -D warnings
    else
      cargo clippy -p "$crate" --all-targets --no-default-features -- -D warnings
    fi
  done
}

run_contract_client_gen_clippy() {
  echo "Running clippy on stylus-proc with contract-client-gen feature..."
  cargo clippy -p stylus-proc --no-default-features --features "contract-client-gen" --all-targets -- -D warnings
}

run_export_abi_clippy() {
  echo "Running clippy on stylus-proc with export-abi feature..."
  cargo clippy -p stylus-proc --no-default-features --features "export-abi" --all-targets -- -D warnings
}

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  usage
fi

case "$1" in
  -h | --help)
    usage
    ;;
  -c | --contract-client-gen)
    run_contract_client_gen_clippy
    ;;
  -e | --export-abi)
    run_export_abi_clippy
    ;;
  -a | --all-excluding-special-features)
    run_all_clippy
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Error: Unknown option $1"
    usage
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

I now have the full accessor mapping. Global `msg::sender()` becomes `self.vm().msg_sender()`, `evm::log` becomes `self.vm().log(event)`, `contract::address()` becomes `self.vm().contract_address()`, `block::timestamp()` becomes `self.vm().block_timestamp()`, and `block::chainid()` becomes `self.vm().chain_id()`. `TestVM` covers the setters motsu used.

content.text: This is a real v0.3.0 test-infrastructure problem, not a macOS quirk. motsu's global storage is shared by contract type across threads, so `cargo test`'s threaded runner can hit "storage is locked" when two tests use the same contract type at once. nextest runs each test in its own process, which is why the nextest baseline passed. The coverage baseline will use `cargo llvm-cov nextest` so it measures the same tests without the shared-storage race. I'll also fix the experiment's imports and rerun it.

content.text: This settles the design question. Route arms come from the impl block's items (`PublicImpl` uses `self.funcs`), not from the trait's default bodies, so default-bodied traits can't route through the SDK's `#[public]` macro. The SDK's router docs mention `#[inherit]` for composing routers, which might give real composition without re-declaring methods. I'll check how it works.

content.text:
Three distinct causes, and all of them are expected from the SDK changes:
1. Public traits must themselves carry `#[public]`, since 0.10 generates a marker method that the impl must match.
2. Some `call` items are now private (`call::Error`, `call::StaticCallContext`).
3. Several globals moved or were removed (`evm`, `msg`, `block`, `contract`), and `call::MethodError` and `call::Call` have moved.

I'll check the SDK's `call` and `stylus-core::calls` exports to find the replacement paths.

The borrow checker also means `Call::new_mutating(self)` has to be bound before `self.vm()` is borrowed. content.text: `#[storage]` generates both `HostAccess` and `VMAccess` for contract types, so helpers can take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` and pass `self`. I'll record these signature decisions in a shared notes file, since they'll drive the rest of the migration. Then I'll clear the simple remaining errors.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/bench/notes && cat > /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md <<'EOF'
# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
Import paths:
  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())

Traits:
  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
EOF

# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)

Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.

Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.

Read first:
- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).

## Ownership
Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).

## What "done" means for your files
1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
     let vm = TestVM::default();
     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
   may change (documented in the report).
7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.

## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
- Check your files only:
    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.

## Git
- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
  or any command that touches other worktrees.

## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.

content.content:
1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13

content.content:
1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).
51

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.

19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).

/*!
# OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus

A library for secure smart contract development written in Rust for
[Arbitrum Stylus](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/gentle-introduction).
This library offers common smart contract primitives and affordances that take
advantage of the nature of Stylus.

## Usage

To start using it, add `openzeppelin-stylus` to your `Cargo.toml`, or simply run
`cargo add openzeppelin-stylus`.

```toml
[dependencies]
openzeppelin-stylus = "x.x.x"
```

We recommend pinning to a specific version -- expect rapid iteration.

Once defined as a dependency, use one of our pre-defined implementations by
importing them:

```ignore
use openzeppelin_stylus::token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20};
use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct MyContract {
    pub erc20: Erc20}

#[public]
#[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
impl MyContract {}

#[public]
impl IErc20 for MyContract {
    type Error = erc20::Error;

    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.total_supply()
    }

    fn balance_of(&self, account: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.balance_of(account)
    }

    fn transfer(
        &mut self,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer(to, value)
    }

    fn allowance(&self, owner: Address, spender: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.allowance(owner, spender)
    }

    fn approve(
        &mut self,
        spender: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.approve(spender, value)
    }

    fn transfer_from(
        &mut self,
        from: Address,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer_from(from, to, value)
    }
}
```

11	/// The expected value returned from [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`].

22	    ///
23	    /// Check [`super::IErc721Receiver`] trait for more details.
24	    interface IErc721ReceiverInterface {
25	        /// See [`super::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`].
26	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
27	        function onERC721Received(
28	            address operator,
29	            address from,

31	            bytes calldata data
32	        ) external returns (bytes4);
33	    }

36	/// [`super::IErc721`] token receiver trait.
37	///
38	/// Interface for any contract that wants to support
39	/// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`]
40	/// and [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from_with_data`] from ERC-721 asset
41	/// contracts.
42	#[interface_id]
43	#[public]
44	pub trait IErc721Receiver {
45	    /// This function is called whenever an [`super::Erc721`] `token_id`
46	    /// token is transferred to this contract via
47	    /// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`] or
48	    /// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from_with_data`].
49	    ///
50	    /// It must return its its Solidity selector to confirm the token transfer.
51	    /// If any other value is returned or the interface is not implemented
52	    /// by the recipient, the transfer will be reverted.
53	    ///
54	    /// # Arguments
55	    ///
56	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
57	    /// * `operator` - Account of the operator.
58	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
59	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
60	    /// * `data` - Additional data with no specified format.
61	    ///
62	    /// # Errors
63	    ///
64	    /// * May return a custom error.
65	    fn on_erc721_received(
66	        &mut self,
67	        operator: Address,
68	        from: Address,
69	        token_id: U256,
70	        data: Bytes,
71	    ) -> Result<B32, Vec<u8>>;
72	}

2	//!
3	//! We have followed general `OpenZeppelin` Contracts guidelines: functions
4	//! revert instead of returning `false` on failure. This behavior is
5	//! nonetheless conventional and does not conflict with the expectations of
6	//! [`Erc20`] applications.

8	
9	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, Address, U256};

27	        /// Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to
28	        /// another (`to`).

30	        /// Note that `value` may be zero.

32	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
33	        event Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value);

45	        /// * `sender` - Address whose tokens are being transferred.
46	        /// * `balance` - Current balance for the interacting account.

48	        #[derive(Debug)]
49	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
50	        error ERC20InsufficientBalance(address sender, uint256 balance, uint256 needed);

52	        ///

321	    /// Sets a `value` number of tokens as the allowance of `spender` over the
322	    /// caller's tokens.
323	    ///
324	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
325	    /// # Arguments
326	    ///
327	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
328	    /// * `owner` - Account that owns the tokens.
329	    /// * `spender` - Account that will spend the tokens.
330	    /// * `emit_event` - Emit an [`Approval`] event flag.
331	    ///
332	    /// # Errors
333	    ///
334	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSpender`] - If the `spender` address is
335	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
336	    ///
337	    /// # Events
338	    ///
339	    /// * [`Approval`].
340	    fn _approve(
341	        &mut self,
342	        owner: Address,
343	        spender: Address,
344	        value: U256,
345	        emit_event: bool,
346	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
347	        if owner.is_zero() {
348	            return Err(Error::InvalidApprover(ERC20InvalidApprover {
349	                approver: Address::ZERO}));
350	        }
351	
352	        if spender.is_zero() {
353	            return Err(Error::InvalidSpender(ERC20InvalidSpender {
354	                spender: Address::ZERO}));
355	        }
356	
357	        self.allowances.setter(owner).insert(spender, value);
358	        if emit_event {
359	            self.vm().log(Approval { owner, spender, value });
360	        }
361	        Ok(true)
362	    }

364	    /// Internal implementation of transferring tokens between two accounts.
365	    ///
366	    /// # Arguments
367	    ///
368	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
369	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
370	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
371	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
372	    ///
373	    /// # Errors
374	    ///
375	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
376	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `to` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
377	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
378	    ///   enough tokens.
379	    ///
380	    /// # Events
381	    ///
382	    /// * [`Transfer`].
383	    fn _transfer(
384	        &mut self,
385	        from: Address,
386	        to: Address,
387	        value: U256,
388	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
389	        if from.is_zero() {
390	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
391	                sender: Address::ZERO}));
392	        }
393	        if to.is_zero() {
394	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
395	                receiver: Address::ZERO}));
396	        }
397	
398	        self._update(from, to, value)?;
399	
400	        Ok(())
401	    }

403	    /// Creates a `value` amount of tokens and assigns them to `account`,
404	    /// by transferring it from [`Address::ZERO`].
405	    ///
406	    /// # Errors
407	    ///
408	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `account` address is
409	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
410	    ///
411	    /// # Events
412	    ///
413	    /// * [`Transfer`].
414	    ///
415	    /// # Panics
416	    ///
417	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
418	    pub fn _mint(
419	        &mut self,
420	        account: Address,
421	        value: U256,
422	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
423	        if account.is_zero() {
424	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
425	                receiver: Address::ZERO}));
426	        }
427	        self._update(Address::ZERO, account, value)
428	    }
429	
430	    /// Transfers a `value` amount of tokens from `from` to `to`, or
431	    /// alternatively mints (or burns) if `from` (or `to`) is the zero address.
432	    ///
433	    /// All customizations to transfers, mints, and burns should be done by
434	    /// using this function.
435	    ///
436	    /// # Arguments
437	    ///
438	    /// * `from` - Owner's address.
439	    /// * `to` - Recipient's address.
440	    /// * `value` - Amount to be transferred.
441	    ///
442	    /// # Errors
443	    ///
444	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
445	    ///   enough tokens.
446	    ///
447	    /// # Events
448	    ///
449	    /// * [`Transfer`].
450	    ///
451	    /// # Panics
452	    ///
453	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`]. It may happen during `mint`
454	    ///   operation.
455	    pub fn _update(
456	        &mut self,
457	        from: Address,
458	        to: Address,
459	        value: U256,
460	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
461	        if from.is_zero() {
462	            // Mint operation. Overflow check required: the rest of the code
463	            // assumes that `total_supply` never overflows.
464	            self.total_supply.add_assign_checked(
465	                value,
466	                "should not exceed `U256::MAX` for `total_supply`",
467	            );
468	        } else {
469	            let from_balance = self.balances.get(from);
470	            if from_balance < value {
471	                return Err(Error::InsufficientBalance(
472	                    ERC20InsufficientBalance {
473	                        sender: from,
474	                        balance: from_balance,
475	                        needed: value},
476	                ));
477	            }
478	            // Overflow not possible:
479	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
480	            self.balances.setter(from).set(from_balance - value);
481	        }
482	
483	        if to.is_zero() {
484	            // Overflow not possible:
485	            // `value` <= `total_supply` or
486	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
487	            self.total_supply.sub_assign_unchecked(value);
488	        } else {
489	            // Overflow not possible:
490	            // `balance_to` + `value` is at most `total_supply`,
491	            // which fits into a `U256`.
492	            self.balances.setter(to).add_assign_unchecked(value);
493	        }
494	
495	        self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, value });
496	
497	        Ok(())
498	    }
499	
500	    /// Destroys a `value` amount of tokens from `account`,
501	    /// lowering the total supply.
502	    ///
503	    /// # Arguments
504	    ///
505	    /// * `account` - Owner's address.
506	    /// * `value` - Amount to be burnt.
507	    ///
508	    /// # Errors
509	    ///
510	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
511	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
512	    ///   enough tokens.
513	    ///
514	    /// # Events
515	    ///
516	    /// * [`Transfer`].
517	    pub fn _burn(
518	        &mut self,
519	        account: Address,
520	        value: U256,
521	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
522	        if account == Address::ZERO {
523	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
524	                sender: Address::ZERO}));
525	        }
526	        self._update(account, Address::ZERO, value)
527	    }
528	
529	    /// Updates `owner`'s allowance for `spender` based on spent `value`.
530	    ///
531	    /// Does not update the allowance value in the case of infinite allowance.
532	    ///
533	    /// # Arguments
534	    ///
535	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
536	    /// * `owner` - Account to transfer tokens from.
537	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
538	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
539	    ///
540	    /// # Errors
541	    ///
542	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientAllowance`] - If not enough allowance is
543	    ///   available.
544	    ///
545	    /// # Events
546	    ///
547	    /// * [`Approval`].
548	    pub fn _spend_allowance(
549	        &mut self,
550	        owner: Address,
551	        spender: Address,
552	        value: U256,
553	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
554	        let current_allowance = self.allowance(owner, spender);
555	        if current_allowance != U256::MAX {
556	            if current_allowance < value {
557	                return Err(Error::InsufficientAllowance(
558	                    ERC20InsufficientAllowance {
559	                        spender,
560	                        allowance: current_allowance,
561	                        needed: value},
562	                ));
563	            }
564	
565	            self._approve(owner, spender, current_allowance - value, false)?;
566	        }
567	
568	        Ok(())
569	    }
570	}

63	/// which is where they will delegate all function calls.

69	#[public]
70	pub trait IUpgradeableBeacon: IBeacon + IOwnable {
71	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
72	    ///
73	    /// # Arguments
74	    ///
75	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
76	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
77	    ///
78	    /// # Errors
79	    ///
80	    /// Implementing contracts should define their own error types for this
81	    /// function. Typically, errors may include:
82	    /// * The caller is not authorized to perform the upgrade.
83	    /// * The new implementation address is invalid (e.g., not a contract).
84	    /// * The upgrade operation failed for contract-specific reasons.
85	    ///
86	    /// The error should be encoded as a [`Vec<u8>`].
87	    fn upgrade_to(
88	        &mut self,
89	        new_implementation: Address,
90	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
91	}

94	#[storage]
95	pub struct UpgradeableBeacon {
96	    /// The address of the implementation contract.
97	    implementation: StorageAddress,
98	    /// The [`Ownable`] contract that owns the beacon.
99	    ownable: Ownable}

104	#[implements(IBeacon, IOwnable)]
105	impl UpgradeableBeacon {
106	    /// Sets the address of the initial implementation, and the initial owner
107	    /// who can upgrade the beacon.
108	    ///
109	    /// # Arguments
110	    ///
111	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
112	    /// * `implementation` - The address of the initial implementation.
113	    ///
114	    /// # Errors
115	    ///
116	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `implementation` is not a
117	    ///   contract.
118	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedAccount`] - If the caller is not the owner.
119	    ///
120	    /// # Events
121	    ///
122	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
123	    #[constructor]
124	    pub fn constructor(
125	        &mut self,
126	        implementation: Address,
127	        initial_owner: Address,
128	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
129	        self.ownable.constructor(initial_owner)?;
130	        self.set_implementation(implementation)?;
131	        Ok(())
132	    }
133	
134	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
135	    ///
136	    /// # Arguments
137	    ///
138	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
139	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
140	    ///
141	    /// # Errors
142	    ///
143	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `new_implementation` is not a
144	    ///   contract.
145	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedAccount`] - If the caller is not the owner.
146	    ///
147	    /// # Events
148	    ///
149	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
150	    pub fn upgrade_to(
151	        &mut self,
152	        new_implementation: Address,
153	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
154	        self.ownable.only_owner()?;
155	        self.set_implementation(new_implementation)
156	    }
157	
158	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
159	    ///
160	    /// # Arguments
161	    ///
162	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
163	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
164	    ///
165	    /// # Errors
166	    ///
167	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `new_implementation` is not a
168	    ///   contract.
169	    ///
170	    /// # Events
171	    ///
172	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
173	    fn set_implementation(
174	        &mut self,
175	        new_implementation: Address,
176	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
177	        if !new_implementation.has_code() {
178	            return Err(Error::InvalidImplementation(
179	                BeaconInvalidImplementation {
180	                    implementation: new_implementation},
181	            ));
182	        }
183	        self.implementation.set(new_implementation);
184	        self.vm().log(Upgraded { implementation: new_implementation });
185	        Ok(())
186	    }
187	}

191	    fn implementation(&self) -> Result<Address, Vec<u8>> {
192	        Ok(self.implementation.get())
193	    }
194	}
