694	    /// Performs an acceptance check for the provided `operator` by calling
695	    /// [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_received`] in case of single token
696	    /// transfer, or [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_batch_received`] in
697	    /// case of batch transfer on the `to` address.
698	    ///
699	    /// The acceptance call is not executed and treated as a no-op if the
700	    /// target address doesn't contain code (i.e. an EOA). Otherwise,
701	    /// the recipient must implement either
702	    /// [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_received`] for single transfer, or
703	    /// [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_batch_received`] for a batch transfer,
704	    /// and return the acceptance value to accept the transfer.
705	    ///
706	    /// # Arguments
707	    ///
708	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
709	    /// * `operator` - Generally the address that initiated the token transfer
710	    ///   (e.g. `self.vm().msg_sender()`).
711	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
712	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
713	    /// * `details` - Details about token transfer, check
714	    ///   [`Erc1155ReceiverData`].
715	    /// * `data` - Additional data with no specified format, sent in call to
716	    ///   `to`.
717	    ///
718	    /// # Errors
719	    ///
720	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
721	    ///   [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_received`] or
722	    ///   [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_batch_received`] haven't returned the
723	    ///   interface id or returned an error.
724	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If
725	    ///   [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_received`] or
726	    ///   [`IErc1155Receiver::on_erc1155_batch_received`] reverted with revert
727	    ///   data.
728	    fn _check_on_erc1155_received(
729	        &mut self,
730	        operator: Address,
731	        from: Address,
732	        to: Address,
733	        details: Erc1155ReceiverData,
734	        data: alloy_primitives::Bytes,
735	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
736	        if !to.has_code() {
737	            return Ok(());
738	        }
739	
740	        let receiver = IErc1155ReceiverInterface::new(to);
741	        let call = Call::new_in(self);
742	        let result = match details.transfer {
743	            Transfer::Single { id, value } => receiver
744	                .on_erc_1155_received(call, operator, from, id, value, data),
745	
746	            Transfer::Batch { ids, values } => receiver
747	                .on_erc_1155_batch_received(
748	                    call, operator, from, ids, values, data,
749	                )};
750	
751	        let id = match result {
752	            Ok(id) => id,
753	            Err(e) => {
754	                if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
755	                    if !reason.is_empty() {
756	                        return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
757	                            InvalidReceiverWithReason {
758	                                reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
759	                                    .to_string()},
760	                        ));
761	                    }
762	                }
763	
764	                // Non-IERC1155Receiver implementer.
765	                return Err(ERC1155InvalidReceiver { receiver: to }.into());
766	            }
767	        };
768	
769	        // Token rejected.
770	        if id != details.receiver_fn_selector {
771	            return Err(ERC1155InvalidReceiver { receiver: to }.into());
772	        }
773	
774	        Ok(())
775	    }

4	//! Defines host environment methods Stylus SDK contracts have access to.
5	extern crate alloc;
6	
7	use alloc::vec::Vec;
8	
9	use alloy_primitives::{Address, B256, U256};
10	use alloy_sol_types::{abi::token::WordToken, SolEvent, TopicList};
11	use dyn_clone::DynClone;
12	
13	/// The host trait defines methods a Stylus contract can use to interact
14	/// with a host environment, such as the EVM. It is a composition
15	/// of traits with different access to host values and modifications.
16	/// Stylus contracts in the SDK have access to a host via the [`HostAccess`] trait for safe access
17	/// to hostios without the need for global invocations. The host trait may be implemented
18	/// by test frameworks as an easier way of mocking hostio invocations for testing
19	/// Stylus contracts.
20	pub trait Host:
21	    CryptographyAccess
22	    + CalldataAccess
23	    + UnsafeDeploymentAccess
24	    + StorageAccess
25	    + UnsafeCallAccess
26	    + BlockAccess
27	    + ChainAccess
28	    + AccountAccess
29	    + MemoryAccess
30	    + MessageAccess
31	    + MeteringAccess
32	    + RawLogAccess
33	    + DynClone
34	{
35	}
36	
37	// Enables cloning of a boxed, host trait object.
38	dyn_clone::clone_trait_object!(Host);
39	
40	/// Defines a trait that allows a Stylus contract to access its host safely.
41	pub trait HostAccess {
42	    /// Host type returned by [`Self::vm()`].
43	    type Host: Host;
44	
45	    /// Provides access to the parametrized host of a contract, giving access
46	    /// to all the desired hostios from the user.
47	    fn vm(&self) -> &Self::Host;
48	}
49	
50	/// Defines a trait that can deny access to a contract router method if a message value is
51	/// passed in while the method is non-payable.
52	pub trait ValueDenier {
53	    fn deny_value(&self, method_name: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
54	}
55	
56	/// Defines a trait that guards whether the constructor was already called.
57	pub trait ConstructorGuard {
58	    fn check_constructor_slot(&self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
59	}
60	
61	/// Provides access to native cryptography extensions provided by
62	/// a Stylus contract host, such as keccak256.
63	pub trait CryptographyAccess {
64	    /// Efficiently computes the [`keccak256`] hash of the given preimage.
65	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SHA3`] opcode.
66	    ///
67	    /// [`keccak256`]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-3
68	    /// [`SHA3`]: https://www.evm.codes/#20
69	    fn native_keccak256(&self, input: &[u8]) -> B256;
70	}
71	
72	/// Provides access to host methods relating to the accessing the calldata
73	/// of a Stylus contract transaction.
74	pub trait CalldataAccess {
75	    /// Reads the program calldata. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
76	    /// [`CALLDATA_COPY`] opcode when requesting the entirety of the current call's calldata.
77	    ///
78	    /// [`CALLDATA_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#37
79	    fn read_args(&self, len: usize) -> Vec<u8>;
80	    /// Copies the bytes of the last EVM call or deployment return result. Does not revert if out of
81	    /// bounds, but rather copies the overlapping portion. The semantics are otherwise equivalent
82	    /// to that of the EVM's [`RETURN_DATA_COPY`] opcode.
83	    ///
84	    /// Returns the number of bytes written.
85	    ///
86	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3e
87	    fn read_return_data(&self, offset: usize, size: Option<usize>) -> Vec<u8>;
88	    /// Returns the length of the last EVM call or deployment return result, or `0` if neither have
89	    /// happened during the program's execution. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
90	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_SIZE`] opcode.
91	    ///
92	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_SIZE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3d
93	    fn return_data_size(&self) -> usize;
94	    /// Writes the final return data. If not called before the program exists, the return data will
95	    /// be 0 bytes long. Note that this hostio does not cause the program to exit, which happens
96	    /// naturally when `user_entrypoint` returns.
97	    fn write_result(&self, data: &[u8]);
98	}
99	
100	/// Provides access to programmatic creation of contracts via the host environment's CREATE
101	/// and CREATE2 opcodes in the EVM.
102	///
103	/// # Safety
104	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
105	/// to create1 and create2 opcodes is needed. Using the methods by themselves will not protect
106	/// against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe contract deployment,
107	/// utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead.
108	pub unsafe trait UnsafeDeploymentAccess {
109	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
110	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
111	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
112	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
113	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
114	    /// for more information on writing init code.
115	    ///
116	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is
117	    /// a function of the sender and nonce. On failure the address will be `0`, `return_data_len`
118	    /// will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read via the
119	    /// `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CREATE`]
120	    /// opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
121	    ///
122	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
123	    /// [`CREATE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f0
124	    ///
125	    /// # Safety
126	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create1 is
127	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
128	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
129	    unsafe fn create1(
130	        &self,
131	        code: *const u8,
132	        code_len: usize,
133	        endowment: *const u8,
134	        contract: *mut u8,
135	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
136	    );
137	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
138	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
139	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
140	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
141	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
142	    /// for more information on writing init code.
143	    ///
144	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is a
145	    /// function of the sender, salt, and init code. On failure the address will be `0`,
146	    /// `return_data_len` will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read
147	    /// via the `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
148	    /// `[CREATE2`] opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
149	    ///
150	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
151	    /// [`CREATE2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f5
152	    ///
153	    /// # Safety
154	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create2 is
155	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
156	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
157	    unsafe fn create2(
158	        &self,
159	        code: *const u8,
160	        code_len: usize,
161	        endowment: *const u8,
162	        salt: *const u8,
163	        contract: *mut u8,
164	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
165	    );
166	}
167	
168	/// Provides access to storage access and mutation via host methods.
169	pub trait StorageAccess {
170	    /// Reads a 32-byte value from permanent storage. Stylus's storage format is identical to
171	    /// that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio is accessing the 32-byte
172	    /// value stored in the EVM state trie at offset `key`, which will be `0` when not previously
173	    /// set. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SLOAD`] opcode.
174	    ///
175	    /// Note: the Stylus VM implements storage caching. This means that repeated calls to the same
176	    /// key will cost less than in the EVM.
177	    ///
178	    /// [`SLOAD`]: https://www.evm.codes/#54
179	    fn storage_load_bytes32(&self, key: U256) -> B256;
180	    /// Writes a 32-byte value to the permanent storage cache. Stylus's storage format is identical
181	    /// to that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio represents storing a
182	    /// 32-byte value into the EVM state trie at offset `key`. Refunds are tabulated exactly as
183	    /// in the EVM. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SSTORE`] opcode.
184	    ///
185	    /// Note: because the value is cached, one must call `flush_cache` to persist it.
186	    ///
187	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
188	    ///
189	    /// # Safety
190	    /// May alias storage.
191	    unsafe fn storage_cache_bytes32(&self, key: U256, value: B256);
192	    /// Persists any dirty values in the storage cache to the EVM state trie, dropping the cache
193	    /// entirely if requested. Analogous to repeated invocations of [`SSTORE`].
194	    ///
195	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
196	    fn flush_cache(&self, clear: bool);
197	}
198	
199	/// Provides access to calling other contracts using host semantics.
200	///
201	/// # Safety
202	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
203	/// to call, static_call, and delegate_call methods is required. Using the methods by themselves
204	/// will not protect against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe
205	/// contract calls, utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead.
206	pub unsafe trait UnsafeCallAccess {
207	    /// Calls the contract at the given address with options for passing value and to limit the
208	    /// amount of gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is
209	    /// nonzero on failure.
210	    ///
211	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
212	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
213	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
214	    /// like to copy.
215	    ///
216	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALL`] opcode, including callvalue
217	    /// stipends and the 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying the `u64::MAX` gas can be used
218	    /// to send as much as possible.
219	    ///
220	    /// [`CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f1
221	    ///
222	    /// # Safety
223	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
224	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
225	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
226	    unsafe fn call_contract(
227	        &self,
228	        to: *const u8,
229	        data: *const u8,
230	        data_len: usize,
231	        value: *const u8,
232	        gas: u64,
233	        outs_len: &mut usize,
234	    ) -> u8;
235	    /// Static calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of gas
236	    /// supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
237	    /// failure.
238	    ///
239	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
240	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
241	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
242	    /// like to copy.
243	    ///
244	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`STATIC_CALL`] opcode, including the
245	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
246	    /// possible.
247	    ///
248	    /// [`STATIC_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#FA
249	    ///
250	    /// # Safety
251	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
252	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
253	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
254	    unsafe fn static_call_contract(
255	        &self,
256	        to: *const u8,
257	        data: *const u8,
258	        data_len: usize,
259	        gas: u64,
260	        outs_len: &mut usize,
261	    ) -> u8;
262	    /// Delegate calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of
263	    /// gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
264	    /// failure.
265	    ///
266	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which
267	    /// can be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that
268	    /// the programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result
269	    /// they'd like to copy.
270	    ///
271	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`DELEGATE_CALL`] opcode, including the
272	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
273	    /// possible.
274	    ///
275	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#F4
276	    ///
277	    /// # Safety
278	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
279	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
280	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
281	    unsafe fn delegate_call_contract(
282	        &self,
283	        to: *const u8,
284	        data: *const u8,
285	        data_len: usize,
286	        gas: u64,
287	        outs_len: &mut usize,
288	    ) -> u8;
289	}
290	
291	/// Provides access to host methods relating to the block a transaction
292	/// to a Stylus contract is included in.
293	pub trait BlockAccess {
294	    /// Gets the basefee of the current block. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
295	    /// [`BASEFEE`] opcode.
296	    ///
297	    /// [`BASEFEE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#48
298	    fn block_basefee(&self) -> U256;
299	    /// Gets the coinbase of the current block, which on Arbitrum chains is the L1 batch poster's
300	    /// address. This differs from Ethereum where the validator including the transaction
301	    /// determines the coinbase.
302	    fn block_coinbase(&self) -> Address;
303	    /// Gets a bounded estimate of the L1 block number at which the Sequencer sequenced the
304	    /// transaction. See [`Block Numbers and Time`] for more information on how this value is
305	    /// determined.
306	    ///
307	    /// [`Block Numbers and Time`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/time
308	    fn block_number(&self) -> u64;
309	    /// Gets a bounded estimate of the Unix timestamp at which the Sequencer sequenced the
310	    /// transaction. See [`Block Numbers and Time`] for more information on how this value is
311	    /// determined.
312	    ///
313	    /// [`Block Numbers and Time`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/time
314	    fn block_timestamp(&self) -> u64;
315	    /// Gets the gas limit of the current block. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
316	    /// [`GAS_LIMIT`] opcode. Note that as of the time of this writing, `evm.codes` incorrectly
317	    /// implies that the opcode returns the gas limit of the current transaction.  When in doubt,
318	    /// consult [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`].
319	    ///
320	    /// [`GAS_LIMIT`]: https://www.evm.codes/#45
321	    /// [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`]: https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf
322	    fn block_gas_limit(&self) -> u64;
323	}
324	
325	/// Provides access to the chain details of the host environment.
326	pub trait ChainAccess {
327	    /// Gets the unique chain identifier of the Arbitrum chain. The semantics are equivalent to
328	    /// that of the EVM's [`CHAIN_ID`] opcode.
329	    ///
330	    /// [`CHAIN_ID`]: https://www.evm.codes/#46
331	    fn chain_id(&self) -> u64;
332	}
333	
334	/// Provides access to account details of addresses of the host environment.
335	pub trait AccountAccess {
336	    /// Gets the ETH balance in wei of the account at the given address.
337	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`BALANCE`] opcode.
338	    ///
339	    /// [`BALANCE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#31
340	    fn balance(&self, account: Address) -> U256;
341	    /// Gets the address of the current program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
342	    /// [`ADDRESS`] opcode.
343	    ///
344	    /// [`ADDRESS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#30
345	    fn contract_address(&self) -> Address;
346	    /// Gets a subset of the code from the account at the given address. The semantics are identical
347	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODE_COPY`] opcode, aside from one small detail: the write to
348	    /// the buffer `dest` will stop after the last byte is written. This is unlike the EVM,
349	    /// which right pads with zeros in this scenario. The return value is the number of bytes
350	    /// written, which allows the caller to detect if this has occurred.
351	    ///
352	    /// [`EXT_CODE_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3C
353	    fn code(&self, account: Address) -> Vec<u8>;
354	    /// Gets the size of the code in bytes at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
355	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODESIZE`].
356	    ///
357	    /// [`EXT_CODESIZE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3B
358	    fn code_size(&self, account: Address) -> usize;
359	    /// Gets the code hash of the account at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
360	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODEHASH`] opcode. Note that the code hash of an account without
361	    /// code will be the empty hash
362	    /// `keccak("") = c5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470`.
363	    ///
364	    /// [`EXT_CODEHASH`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3F
365	    fn code_hash(&self, account: Address) -> B256;
366	}
367	
368	/// Provides the ability to pay for memory growth of a Stylus contract.
369	pub trait MemoryAccess {
370	    /// The `entrypoint!` macro handles importing this hostio, which is required if the
371	    /// program's memory grows. Otherwise compilation through the `ArbWasm` precompile will revert.
372	    /// Internally the Stylus VM forces calls to this hostio whenever new WASM pages are allocated.
373	    /// Calls made voluntarily will unproductively consume gas.
374	    fn pay_for_memory_grow(&self, pages: u16);
375	}
376	
377	/// Provides access to transaction details of a Stylus contract.
378	pub trait MessageAccess {
379	    /// Gets the address of the account that called the program. For normal L2-to-L2 transactions
380	    /// the semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALLER`] opcode, including in cases
381	    /// arising from [`DELEGATE_CALL`].
382	    ///
383	    /// For L1-to-L2 retryable ticket transactions, the top-level sender's address will be aliased.
384	    /// See [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`] for more information on how this works.
385	    ///
386	    /// [`CALLER`]: https://www.evm.codes/#33
387	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f4
388	    /// [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/arbos/l1-to-l2-messaging#address-aliasing
389	    fn msg_sender(&self) -> Address;
390	    /// Whether the current call is reentrant.
391	    fn msg_reentrant(&self) -> bool;
392	    /// Get the ETH value in wei sent to the program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
393	    /// EVM's [`CALLVALUE`] opcode.
394	    ///
395	    /// [`CALLVALUE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#34
396	    fn msg_value(&self) -> U256;
397	    /// Gets the top-level sender of the transaction. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
398	    /// EVM's [`ORIGIN`] opcode.
399	    ///
400	    /// [`ORIGIN`]: https://www.evm.codes/#32
401	    fn tx_origin(&self) -> Address;
402	}
403	
404	/// Provides access to metering values such as EVM gas and Stylus ink used and remaining,
405	/// as well as details of their prices based on the host environment.
406	pub trait MeteringAccess {
407	    /// Gets the amount of gas left after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics are
408	    /// equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode.
409	    ///
410	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
411	    fn evm_gas_left(&self) -> u64;
412	    /// Gets the amount of ink remaining after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics
413	    /// are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode, except the units are in ink. See
414	    /// [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on Stylus's compute pricing.
415	    ///
416	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
417	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
418	    fn evm_ink_left(&self) -> u64;
419	    /// Gets the gas price in wei per gas, which on Arbitrum chains equals the basefee. The
420	    /// semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS_PRICE`] opcode.
421	    ///
422	    /// [`GAS_PRICE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3A
423	    fn tx_gas_price(&self) -> U256;
424	    /// Gets the price of ink in evm gas basis points. See [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on
425	    /// Stylus's compute-pricing model. Arbitrum enforces a minimum gas price floor, so tx ink
426	    /// price should always return a value greater than zero.
427	    ///
428	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
429	    fn tx_ink_price(&self) -> u32;
430	
431	    /// Computes the units of gas per a specified amount of ink.
432	    fn ink_to_gas(&self, ink: u64) -> u64 {
433	        let price = self.tx_ink_price();
434	        if price == 0 {
435	            return 0;
436	        }
437	        ink / price as u64
438	    }
439	
440	    /// Computes the units of ink per a specified amount of gas.
441	    fn gas_to_ink(&self, gas: u64) -> u64 {
442	        gas.saturating_mul(self.tx_ink_price().into())
443	    }
444	}
445	
446	/// Provides access to the ability to emit logs from a Stylus contract.
447	pub trait RawLogAccess {
448	    /// Emits an EVM log with the given number of topics and data, the first bytes of which should
449	    /// be the 32-byte-aligned topic data. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
450	    /// [`LOG0`], [`LOG1`], [`LOG2`], [`LOG3`], and [`LOG4`] opcodes based on the number of topics
451	    /// specified. Requesting more than `4` topics will induce a revert.
452	    ///
453	    /// [`LOG0`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a0
454	    /// [`LOG1`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a1
455	    /// [`LOG2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a2
456	    /// [`LOG3`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a3
457	    /// [`LOG4`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a4
458	    fn emit_log(&self, input: &[u8], num_topics: usize);
459	    /// Emits a raw log from topics and data.
460	    fn raw_log(&self, topics: &[B256], data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), &'static str>;
461	}
462	
463	/// Provides access to the ability to emit typed logs from a Stylus contract.
464	pub trait LogAccess: RawLogAccess {
465	    /// Emits a typed alloy log.
466	    ///
467	    /// ```rust,ignore
468	    /// sol! {
469	    ///    event Transfer(
470	    ///        address indexed from,
471	    ///        address indexed to,
472	    ///        uint256 indexed token_id
473	    ///    );
474	    /// }
475	    ///
476	    /// self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, token_id });
477	    /// ```
478	    fn log<T: SolEvent>(&self, event: T) {
479	        // According to the alloy docs, encode_topics_raw fails only if the array is too small
480	
481	        let mut topics = [WordToken::default(); 4];
482	        event.encode_topics_raw(&mut topics).unwrap();
483	
484	        let count = T::TopicList::COUNT;
485	        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(32 * count);
486	        for topic in &topics[..count] {
487	            bytes.extend_from_slice(topic.as_slice());
488	        }
489	        event.encode_data_to(&mut bytes);
490	        self.emit_log(&bytes, count)
491	    }
492	}
493	
494	impl<T: RawLogAccess> LogAccess for T {}

1	//! An upgradeability mechanism designed for UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy
2	//! Standard) proxies as defined in [ERC-1822].
3	//!
4	//! [ERC-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
5	//!
6	//! The functions included here can perform an upgrade of an
7	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`], when this contract is set as the implementation
8	//! behind such a proxy.
9	//!
10	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`]: crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy
11	
12	// The contract is covered 100% via e2e tests, but this cannot be displayed due
13	// to the inability llvm-cov to display e2e coverage. Marking this with
14	// coverage(off) to avoid a false negative.
15	//
16	// TODO: remove this attribute when 100% coverage can be achieved through unit
17	// tests.
18	#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
19	
20	pub use alloc::{string::String, vec, vec::Vec};
21	
22	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B256, uint, Address, U256, U32};
23	use stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError;
24	use alloy_sol_types::SolCall;
25	pub use sol::*;
26	use stylus_sdk::{abi::Bytes, prelude::*, storage::{StorageBool, StorageU32}};
27	
28	use crate::{
29	    proxy::{
30	        erc1967::{
31	            self,
32	            utils::{
33	                ERC1967InvalidAdmin, ERC1967InvalidBeacon,
34	                ERC1967InvalidImplementation, ERC1967NonPayable, Erc1967Utils,
35	                IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT}},
36	        utils::erc1822::{Erc1822ProxiableInterface, IErc1822Proxiable}},
37	    utils::{
38	        address::{self, AddressUtils},
39	        storage_slot::StorageSlot}};
40	
41	/// The version of the upgrade interface of the contract.
42	pub const UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION: &str = "5.0.0";
43	
44	/// The version number of the logic contract.
45	pub const VERSION_NUMBER: U32 = uint!(1_U32);
46	
47	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
48	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) execution
49	/// contexts.
50	///
51	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
52	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
53	///
54	/// Behavior:
55	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
56	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), `logic_flag ==
57	///   false` (i.e., the proxy’s storage does not contain this
58	///   implementation-only flag).
59	///
60	/// Security notes:
61	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
62	///
63	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
64	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
65	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
66	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
67	        .finalize();
68	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
69	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
70	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
71	
72	    B256::new(slot)
73	};
74	
75	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
76	mod sol {
77	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
78	
79	    sol! {
80	        /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
81	        #[derive(Debug)]
82	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
83	        error UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext();
84	
85	        /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
86	        ///
87	        /// * `slot` - The unsupported UUID returned by the implementation.
88	        #[derive(Debug)]
89	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
90	        error UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID(bytes32 slot);
91	
92	        /// The contract is already initialized.
93	        #[derive(Debug)]
94	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
95	        error InvalidInitialization();
96	
97	        /// The version is not greater than the current version.
98	        ///
99	        /// * `current_version` - The current version.
100	        #[derive(Debug)]
101	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
102	        error InvalidVersion(uint32 current_version);
103	
104	        interface UUPSUpgradeableInterface {
105	            function setVersion() external;
106	        }
107	    }
108	}
109	
110	/// An [`UUPSUpgradeable`] error.
111	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
112	pub enum Error {
113	    /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
114	    UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext),
115	    /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
116	    UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID),
117	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
118	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
119	    InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation),
120	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `admin` of the
121	    /// proxy is invalid.
122	    InvalidAdmin(ERC1967InvalidAdmin),
123	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `beacon`
124	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
125	    InvalidBeacon(ERC1967InvalidBeacon),
126	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
127	    /// sees [`stylus_sdk::self.vm().msg_value()`] > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]
128	    /// that may be lost.
129	    NonPayable(ERC1967NonPayable),
130	    /// There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).
131	    EmptyCode(address::AddressEmptyCode),
132	    /// A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.
133	    FailedCall(address::FailedCall),
134	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the
135	    /// [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] failed.
136	    FailedCallWithReason(address::FailedCallWithReason),
137	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the contract is already
138	    /// initialized.
139	    InvalidInitialization(InvalidInitialization),
140	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the version is not greater
141	    /// than the current version.
142	    InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion)}

237	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
238	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
239	///
240	/// # Overview
241	///
242	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
243	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
244	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
245	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
246	///
247	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
248	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
249	/// upgrade flow.
250	///
251	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
252	///
253	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
254	///
255	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
256	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
257	/// slot:
258	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
259	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
260	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
261	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
262	///
263	/// ## Initialization Pattern
264	///
265	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
266	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
267	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
268	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
269	///   `only_proxy()`.
270	///
271	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
272	///
273	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
274	///
275	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
276	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
277	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
278	///    the proxy.
279	///
280	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
281	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
282	/// unauthorized upgrades.
283	///
284	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
285	///
286	/// ## Common Mistakes
287	///
288	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
289	///   number constant does not increase.
290	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
291	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
292	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
293	///
294	/// ## Security Considerations
295	///
296	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
297	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
298	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
299	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
300	///
301	/// # Usage
302	///
303	/// ```rust
304	/// extern crate alloc;
305	///
306	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
307	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
308	///
309	/// #[storage]
310	/// #[entrypoint]
311	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
312	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
313	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
314	///
315	///     // Your contract's state variables
316	///     value: StorageU256,
317	///     // ...
318	/// }
319	///
320	/// #[public]
321	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
322	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
323	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
324	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
325	///     }
326	///
327	///     // Your contract's functions
328	/// }
329	/// ```
330	///
331	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
332	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
333	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
334	#[storage]
335	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
336	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
337	    pub version: StorageU32}
338	
339	#[public]
340	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
341	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
342	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
343	    ///
344	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
345	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
346	    ///
347	    /// # Arguments
348	    ///
349	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
350	    #[constructor]
351	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
352	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
353	    }
354	
355	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
356	    /// (initializer-like).
357	    ///
358	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
359	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
360	    ///
361	    /// # Arguments
362	    ///
363	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
364	    ///
365	    /// # Errors
366	    ///
367	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
368	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
369	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
370	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
371	    ///
372	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
373	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
374	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
375	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
376	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
377	            ));
378	        }
379	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
380	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
381	                current_version: self.version.get().to()}));
382	        }
383	
384	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
385	        Ok(())
386	    }
387	}

389	#[public]
390	impl IUUPSUpgradeable for UUPSUpgradeable {
391	    fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String {
392	        UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION.into()
393	    }
394	
395	    #[payable]
396	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
397	        &mut self,
398	        new_implementation: Address,
399	        data: Bytes,
400	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
401	        self.only_proxy()?;
402	        self._upgrade_to_and_call_uups(new_implementation, &data)?;
403	
404	        let data_set_version =
405	            UUPSUpgradeableInterface::setVersionCall {}.abi_encode();
406	        AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
407	            self,
408	            new_implementation,
409	            &data_set_version,
410	        )?;
411	
412	        Ok(())
413	    }
414	}

416	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
417	    /// Get the logic contract version.
418	    ///
419	    /// # Arguments
420	    ///
421	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
422	    #[must_use]
423	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
424	        VERSION_NUMBER
425	    }
426	
427	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
428	    ///
429	    /// # Arguments
430	    ///
431	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
432	    #[must_use]
433	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
434	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
435	    }
436	
437	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
438	    ///
439	    /// # Arguments
440	    ///
441	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
442	    #[must_use]
443	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
444	        self.logic_flag().get()
445	    }
446	
447	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
448	    ///
449	    /// Checks:
450	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] (checked
451	    ///    via `!self.is_logic()`).
452	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
453	    ///    non-zero).
454	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
455	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
456	    ///
457	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
458	    ///
459	    /// # Security Implications
460	    ///
461	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
462	    /// implementation contract.
463	    ///
464	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
465	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
466	    ///
467	    /// # Edge Cases
468	    ///
469	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
470	    ///   check
471	    ///
472	    /// # Arguments
473	    ///
474	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
475	    ///
476	    /// # Errors
477	    ///
478	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
479	    ///   not met
480	    ///
481	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
482	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
483	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
484	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
485	        if self.is_logic()
486	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation() == Address::ZERO
487	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
488	        {
489	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
490	        } else {
491	            Ok(())
492	        }
493	    }
494	
495	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
496	    /// [`delegate_call`].
497	    ///
498	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
499	    /// but not through proxies.
500	    ///
501	    /// # Arguments
502	    ///
503	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
504	    ///
505	    /// # Errors
506	    ///
507	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
508	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
509	    ///
510	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
511	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
512	        if self.is_logic() {
513	            Ok(())
514	        } else {
515	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
516	        }
517	    }
518	}

528	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
529	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
530	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
531	    ///
532	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
533	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
534	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
535	    ///
536	    /// # Arguments
537	    ///
538	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
539	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
540	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
541	    ///
542	    /// # Errors
543	    ///
544	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
545	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
546	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
547	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
548	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
549	    ///   not designed to handle it.
550	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
551	    ///   address.
552	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
553	    ///   new implementation fails.
554	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
555	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
556	    ///
557	    /// # Events
558	    ///
559	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the
560	    ///   implementation is upgraded.
561	    ///
562	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
563	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
564	        &mut self,
565	        new_implementation: Address,
566	        data: &Bytes,
567	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
568	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
569	            .proxiable_uuid(Call::new_in(self))
570	            .map_err(|_e| {
571	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
572	                    implementation: new_implementation})
573	            })?;
574	
575	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
576	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
577	                .map_err(Error::from)
578	        } else {
579	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
580	                slot}))
581	        }
582	    }
583	}

/*!
# OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus

A library for secure smart contract development written in Rust for
[Arbitrum Stylus](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/gentle-introduction).
This library offers common smart contract primitives and affordances that take
advantage of the nature of Stylus.

## Usage

To start using it, add `openzeppelin-stylus` to your `Cargo.toml`, or simply run
`cargo add openzeppelin-stylus`.

```toml
[dependencies]
openzeppelin-stylus = "x.x.x"
```

We recommend pinning to a specific version -- expect rapid iteration.

Once defined as a dependency, use one of our pre-defined implementations by
importing them:

```ignore
use openzeppelin_stylus::token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20};
use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct MyContract {
    pub erc20: Erc20}

#[public]
#[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
impl MyContract {}

#[public]
impl IErc20 for MyContract {
    type Error = erc20::Error;

    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.total_supply()
    }

    fn balance_of(&self, account: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.balance_of(account)
    }

    fn transfer(
        &mut self,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer(to, value)
    }

    fn allowance(&self, owner: Address, spender: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.allowance(owner, spender)
    }

    fn approve(
        &mut self,
        spender: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.approve(spender, value)
    }

    fn transfer_from(
        &mut self,
        from: Address,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer_from(from, to, value)
    }
}
```
*/

16	/// ```rust,ignore

18	///     fn supports_interface(&self, interface_id: B32) -> bool {

30	    /// `interface_id`. See the corresponding [ERC] to learn more about how

1	//! `ArbOS` precompiles wrapper enabling easier invocation.
2	
3	use alloy_primitives::{Address, B256};
4	use primitives::ecrecover::Error;
5	use stylus_sdk::prelude::*;
6	
7	use crate::utils::cryptography::ecdsa::recover;
8	
9	mod p256_verify;
10	
11	use p256_verify::p256_verify;
12	pub use p256_verify::P256_VERIFY_ADDRESS;
13	
14	/// Precompile primitives.
15	pub mod primitives {
16	    /// The `ecRecover` precompile primitives.
17	    ///
18	    /// This module provides the cryptographic primitives needed for the
19	    /// `ecRecover` precompile, which recovers the signer address from an
20	    /// ECDSA signature and message hash.
21	    ///
22	    /// Re-exports selected ECDSA types and constants specifically relevant
23	    /// to the ecrecover operation.
24	    pub mod ecrecover {
25	        pub use crate::utils::cryptography::ecdsa::{
26	            ECDSAInvalidSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignatureS, EcRecoverData,
27	            Error, ECRECOVER_ADDR, SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND};
28	    }
29	}
30	
31	/// Trait providing access to Arbitrum precompiles for Stylus contracts.
32	///
33	/// This trait wraps complex precompile invocations to provide a clean,
34	/// ergonomic interface for calling Arbitrum's built-in cryptographic functions
35	/// and utilities from within Stylus smart contracts.
36	///
37	/// Precompiles are pre-deployed contracts at fixed addresses that implement
38	/// commonly used cryptographic operations and other utilities. They execute
39	/// natively in the Arbitrum runtime for better performance compared to
40	/// implementing these operations in contract code.
41	///
42	/// See: <https://docs.arbitrum.io/build-decentralized-apps/precompiles/overview>
43	///
44	/// # Usage
45	///
46	/// Implement this trait for your contract storage type to gain access to
47	/// precompile functionality:
48	///
49	/// ```rust,ignore
50	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::utils::cryptography::Precompiles;
51	///
52	/// #[storage]
53	/// #[entrypoint]
54	/// struct MyContract {
55	///     // your fields...
56	/// }
57	///
58	/// // The `Precompiles` trait is automatically implemented for all
59	/// // contracts annotated with `#[entrypoint]` or that implement
60	/// // `stylus_sdk::prelude::TopLevelStorage`.
61	///
62	/// #[public]
63	/// impl MyContract {
64	///     fn verify_signature(&mut self, msg_hash: B256, sig: (u8, B256, B256)) -> Result<Address, Error> {
65	///         let (v, r, s) = sig;
66	///         self.ec_recover(msg_hash, v, r, s)
67	///     }
68	/// }
69	/// ```
70	///
71	/// # Error Handling
72	///
73	/// Precompile methods return `Result` types to handle both invalid inputs and
74	/// precompile execution failures. Always handle these errors appropriately
75	/// in your contract logic.
76	pub trait Precompiles: TopLevelStorage {
77	    /// Recovers the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) using an
78	    /// ECDSA signature (v, r, s).
79	    ///
80	    /// Wrapper around the `ecRecover` precompile.
81	    ///
82	    /// # Arguments
83	    ///
84	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
85	    /// * `hash` - Hash of the message.
86	    /// * `v` - `v` value from the signature.
87	    /// * `r` - `r` value from the signature.
88	    /// * `s` - `s` value from the signature.
89	    ///
90	    /// # Errors
91	    ///
92	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignatureS`] - If the `s` value is grater than
93	    ///   [`primitives::ecrecover::SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND`].
94	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignature`] - If the recovered address is
95	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
96	    ///
97	    /// # Panics
98	    ///
99	    /// * If the `ecRecover` precompile fails to execute.
100	    fn ec_recover(
101	        &self,
102	        hash: B256,
103	        v: u8,
104	        r: B256,
105	        s: B256,
106	    ) -> Result<Address, Error>;
107	
108	    /// Performs signature verifications in the `secp256r1` elliptic curve.
109	    ///
110	    /// Wrapper around the `P256VERIFY` precompile introduced in [RIP-7212].
111	    ///
112	    /// [RIP-7212]: https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/blob/723155c3d86427412b5bc0f98ad1e4791ea7347f/RIPS/rip-7212.md
113	    ///
114	    /// # Arguments
115	    ///
116	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
117	    /// * `hash` - Signed data hash.
118	    /// * `r` - `r` component of the signature.
119	    /// * `s` - `s` component of the signature.
120	    /// * `x` - `x` coordinate of the public key.
121	    /// * `y` - `y` coordinate of the public key.
122	    fn p256_verify(
123	        &self,
124	        hash: B256,
125	        r: B256,
126	        s: B256,
127	        x: B256,
128	        y: B256,
129	    ) -> bool;
130	}
131	
132	impl<T: TopLevelStorage> Precompiles for T {
133	    fn ec_recover(
134	        &self,
135	        hash: B256,
136	        v: u8,
137	        r: B256,
138	        s: B256,
139	    ) -> Result<Address, Error> {
140	        recover(self, hash, v, r, s)
141	    }
142	
143	    fn p256_verify(
144	        &self,
145	        hash: B256,
146	        r: B256,
147	        s: B256,
148	        x: B256,
149	        y: B256,
150	    ) -> bool {
151	        p256_verify(self, hash, r, s, x, y)
152	    }
153	}

4	//! Defines host environment methods Stylus SDK contracts have access to.
5	extern crate alloc;
6	
7	use alloc::vec::Vec;
8	
9	use alloy_primitives::{Address, B256, U256};
10	use alloy_sol_types::{abi::token::WordToken, SolEvent, TopicList};
11	use dyn_clone::DynClone;
12	
13	/// The host trait defines methods a Stylus contract can use to interact
14	/// with a host environment, such as the EVM. It is a composition
15	/// of traits with different access to host values and modifications.
16	/// Stylus contracts in the SDK have access to a host via the [`HostAccess`] trait for safe access
17	/// to hostios without the need for global invocations. The host trait may be implemented
18	/// by test frameworks as an easier way of mocking hostio invocations for testing
19	/// Stylus contracts.
20	pub trait Host:
21	    CryptographyAccess
22	    + CalldataAccess
23	    + UnsafeDeploymentAccess
24	    + StorageAccess
25	    + UnsafeCallAccess
26	    + BlockAccess
27	    + ChainAccess
28	    + AccountAccess
29	    + MemoryAccess
30	    + MessageAccess
31	    + MeteringAccess
32	    + RawLogAccess
33	    + DynClone
34	{
35	}
36	
37	// Enables cloning of a boxed, host trait object.
38	dyn_clone::clone_trait_object!(Host);
39	
40	/// Defines a trait that allows a Stylus contract to access its host safely.
41	pub trait HostAccess {
42	    /// Host type returned by [`Self::vm()`].
43	    type Host: Host;
44	
45	    /// Provides access to the parametrized host of a contract, giving access
46	    /// to all the desired hostios from the user.
47	    fn vm(&self) -> &Self::Host;
48	}
49	
50	/// Defines a trait that can deny access to a contract router method if a message value is
51	/// passed in while the method is non-payable.
52	pub trait ValueDenier {
53	    fn deny_value(&self, method_name: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
54	}
55	
56	/// Defines a trait that guards whether the constructor was already called.
57	pub trait ConstructorGuard {
58	    fn check_constructor_slot(&self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
59	}
60	
61	/// Provides access to native cryptography extensions provided by
62	/// a Stylus contract host, such as keccak256.
63	pub trait CryptographyAccess {
64	    /// Efficiently computes the [`keccak256`] hash of the given preimage.
65	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SHA3`] opcode.
66	    ///
67	    /// [`keccak256`]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-3
68	    /// [`SHA3`]: https://www.evm.codes/#20
69	    fn native_keccak256(&self, input: &[u8]) -> B256;
70	}
71	
72	/// Provides access to host methods relating to the accessing the calldata
73	/// of a Stylus contract transaction.
74	pub trait CalldataAccess {
75	    /// Reads the program calldata. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
76	    /// [`CALLDATA_COPY`] opcode when requesting the entirety of the current call's calldata.
77	    ///
78	    /// [`CALLDATA_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#37
79	    fn read_args(&self, len: usize) -> Vec<u8>;
80	    /// Copies the bytes of the last EVM call or deployment return result. Does not revert if out of
81	    /// bounds, but rather copies the overlapping portion. The semantics are otherwise equivalent
82	    /// to that of the EVM's [`RETURN_DATA_COPY`] opcode.
83	    ///
84	    /// Returns the number of bytes written.
85	    ///
86	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3e
87	    fn read_return_data(&self, offset: usize, size: Option<usize>) -> Vec<u8>;
88	    /// Returns the length of the last EVM call or deployment return result, or `0` if neither have
89	    /// happened during the program's execution. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
90	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_SIZE`] opcode.
91	    ///
92	    /// [`RETURN_DATA_SIZE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3d
93	    fn return_data_size(&self) -> usize;
94	    /// Writes the final return data. If not called before the program exists, the return data will
95	    /// be 0 bytes long. Note that this hostio does not cause the program to exit, which happens
96	    /// naturally when `user_entrypoint` returns.
97	    fn write_result(&self, data: &[u8]);
98	}
99	
100	/// Provides access to programmatic creation of contracts via the host environment's CREATE
101	/// and CREATE2 opcodes in the EVM.
102	///
103	/// # Safety
104	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
105	/// to create1 and create2 opcodes is needed. Using the methods by themselves will not protect
106	/// against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe contract deployment,
107	/// utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead.
108	pub unsafe trait UnsafeDeploymentAccess {
109	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
110	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
111	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
112	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
113	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
114	    /// for more information on writing init code.
115	    ///
116	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is
117	    /// a function of the sender and nonce. On failure the address will be `0`, `return_data_len`
118	    /// will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read via the
119	    /// `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CREATE`]
120	    /// opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
121	    ///
122	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
123	    /// [`CREATE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f0
124	    ///
125	    /// # Safety
126	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create1 is
127	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
128	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
129	    unsafe fn create1(
130	        &self,
131	        code: *const u8,
132	        code_len: usize,
133	        endowment: *const u8,
134	        contract: *mut u8,
135	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
136	    );
137	    /// Deploys a new contract using the init code provided, which the EVM executes to construct
138	    /// the code of the newly deployed contract. The init code must be written in EVM bytecode, but
139	    /// the code it deploys can be that of a Stylus program. The code returned will be treated as
140	    /// WASM if it begins with the EOF-inspired header `0xEFF0`. Otherwise the code will be
141	    /// interpreted as that of a traditional EVM-style contract. See [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]
142	    /// for more information on writing init code.
143	    ///
144	    /// On success, this hostio returns the address of the newly created account whose address is a
145	    /// function of the sender, salt, and init code. On failure the address will be `0`,
146	    /// `return_data_len` will store the length of the revert data, the bytes of which can be read
147	    /// via the `read_return_data` hostio. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
148	    /// `[CREATE2`] opcode, which notably includes the exact address returned.
149	    ///
150	    /// [`Deploying Stylus Programs`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/quickstart
151	    /// [`CREATE2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f5
152	    ///
153	    /// # Safety
154	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to create2 is
155	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
156	    /// Utilize a [`RawDeploy`] struct instead for safety.
157	    unsafe fn create2(
158	        &self,
159	        code: *const u8,
160	        code_len: usize,
161	        endowment: *const u8,
162	        salt: *const u8,
163	        contract: *mut u8,
164	        revert_data_len: *mut usize,
165	    );
166	}
167	
168	/// Provides access to storage access and mutation via host methods.
169	pub trait StorageAccess {
170	    /// Reads a 32-byte value from permanent storage. Stylus's storage format is identical to
171	    /// that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio is accessing the 32-byte
172	    /// value stored in the EVM state trie at offset `key`, which will be `0` when not previously
173	    /// set. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SLOAD`] opcode.
174	    ///
175	    /// Note: the Stylus VM implements storage caching. This means that repeated calls to the same
176	    /// key will cost less than in the EVM.
177	    ///
178	    /// [`SLOAD`]: https://www.evm.codes/#54
179	    fn storage_load_bytes32(&self, key: U256) -> B256;
180	    /// Writes a 32-byte value to the permanent storage cache. Stylus's storage format is identical
181	    /// to that of the EVM. This means that, under the hood, this hostio represents storing a
182	    /// 32-byte value into the EVM state trie at offset `key`. Refunds are tabulated exactly as
183	    /// in the EVM. The semantics, then, are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`SSTORE`] opcode.
184	    ///
185	    /// Note: because the value is cached, one must call `flush_cache` to persist it.
186	    ///
187	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
188	    ///
189	    /// # Safety
190	    /// May alias storage.
191	    unsafe fn storage_cache_bytes32(&self, key: U256, value: B256);
192	    /// Persists any dirty values in the storage cache to the EVM state trie, dropping the cache
193	    /// entirely if requested. Analogous to repeated invocations of [`SSTORE`].
194	    ///
195	    /// [`SSTORE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#55
196	    fn flush_cache(&self, clear: bool);
197	}
198	
199	/// Provides access to calling other contracts using host semantics.
200	///
201	/// # Safety
202	/// These methods should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access
203	/// to call, static_call, and delegate_call methods is required. Using the methods by themselves
204	/// will not protect against reentrancy safety, storage aliasing, or cache flushing. For safe
205	/// contract calls, utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead.
206	pub unsafe trait UnsafeCallAccess {
207	    /// Calls the contract at the given address with options for passing value and to limit the
208	    /// amount of gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is
209	    /// nonzero on failure.
210	    ///
211	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
212	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
213	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
214	    /// like to copy.
215	    ///
216	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALL`] opcode, including callvalue
217	    /// stipends and the 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying the `u64::MAX` gas can be used
218	    /// to send as much as possible.
219	    ///
220	    /// [`CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f1
221	    ///
222	    /// # Safety
223	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
224	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
225	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
226	    unsafe fn call_contract(
227	        &self,
228	        to: *const u8,
229	        data: *const u8,
230	        data_len: usize,
231	        value: *const u8,
232	        gas: u64,
233	        outs_len: &mut usize,
234	    ) -> u8;
235	    /// Static calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of gas
236	    /// supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
237	    /// failure.
238	    ///
239	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which can
240	    /// be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that the
241	    /// programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result they'd
242	    /// like to copy.
243	    ///
244	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`STATIC_CALL`] opcode, including the
245	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
246	    /// possible.
247	    ///
248	    /// [`STATIC_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#FA
249	    ///
250	    /// # Safety
251	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
252	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
253	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
254	    unsafe fn static_call_contract(
255	        &self,
256	        to: *const u8,
257	        data: *const u8,
258	        data_len: usize,
259	        gas: u64,
260	        outs_len: &mut usize,
261	    ) -> u8;
262	    /// Delegate calls the contract at the given address, with the option to limit the amount of
263	    /// gas supplied. The return status indicates whether the call succeeded, and is nonzero on
264	    /// failure.
265	    ///
266	    /// In both cases `return_data_len` will store the length of the result, the bytes of which
267	    /// can be read via the `read_return_data` hostio. The bytes are not returned directly so that
268	    /// the programmer can potentially save gas by choosing which subset of the return result
269	    /// they'd like to copy.
270	    ///
271	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`DELEGATE_CALL`] opcode, including the
272	    /// 63/64 gas rule. This means that supplying `u64::MAX` gas can be used to send as much as
273	    /// possible.
274	    ///
275	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#F4
276	    ///
277	    /// # Safety
278	    /// This method should only be used in advanced cases when lowest-level access to calls is
279	    /// required. Safe usage needs to consider reentrancy, storage aliasing, and cache flushing.
280	    /// Utilize a [`RawCall`] struct instead for safety.
281	    unsafe fn delegate_call_contract(
282	        &self,
283	        to: *const u8,
284	        data: *const u8,
285	        data_len: usize,
286	        gas: u64,
287	        outs_len: &mut usize,
288	    ) -> u8;
289	}
290	
291	/// Provides access to host methods relating to the block a transaction
292	/// to a Stylus contract is included in.
293	pub trait BlockAccess {
294	    /// Gets the basefee of the current block. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
295	    /// [`BASEFEE`] opcode.
296	    ///
297	    /// [`BASEFEE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#48
298	    fn block_basefee(&self) -> U256;
299	    /// Gets the coinbase of the current block, which on Arbitrum chains is the L1 batch poster's
300	    /// address. This differs from Ethereum where the validator including the transaction
301	    /// determines the coinbase.
302	    fn block_coinbase(&self) -> Address;
303	    /// Gets a bounded estimate of the L1 block number at which the Sequencer sequenced the
304	    /// transaction. See [`Block Numbers and Time`] for more information on how this value is
305	    /// determined.
306	    ///
307	    /// [`Block Numbers and Time`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/time
308	    fn block_number(&self) -> u64;
309	    /// Gets a bounded estimate of the Unix timestamp at which the Sequencer sequenced the
310	    /// transaction. See [`Block Numbers and Time`] for more information on how this value is
311	    /// determined.
312	    ///
313	    /// [`Block Numbers and Time`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/time
314	    fn block_timestamp(&self) -> u64;
315	    /// Gets the gas limit of the current block. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
316	    /// [`GAS_LIMIT`] opcode. Note that as of the time of this writing, `evm.codes` incorrectly
317	    /// implies that the opcode returns the gas limit of the current transaction.  When in doubt,
318	    /// consult [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`].
319	    ///
320	    /// [`GAS_LIMIT`]: https://www.evm.codes/#45
321	    /// [`The Ethereum Yellow Paper`]: https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf
322	    fn block_gas_limit(&self) -> u64;
323	}
324	
325	/// Provides access to the chain details of the host environment.
326	pub trait ChainAccess {
327	    /// Gets the unique chain identifier of the Arbitrum chain. The semantics are equivalent to
328	    /// that of the EVM's [`CHAIN_ID`] opcode.
329	    ///
330	    /// [`CHAIN_ID`]: https://www.evm.codes/#46
331	    fn chain_id(&self) -> u64;
332	}
333	
334	/// Provides access to account details of addresses of the host environment.
335	pub trait AccountAccess {
336	    /// Gets the ETH balance in wei of the account at the given address.
337	    /// The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`BALANCE`] opcode.
338	    ///
339	    /// [`BALANCE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#31
340	    fn balance(&self, account: Address) -> U256;
341	    /// Gets the address of the current program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
342	    /// [`ADDRESS`] opcode.
343	    ///
344	    /// [`ADDRESS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#30
345	    fn contract_address(&self) -> Address;
346	    /// Gets a subset of the code from the account at the given address. The semantics are identical
347	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODE_COPY`] opcode, aside from one small detail: the write to
348	    /// the buffer `dest` will stop after the last byte is written. This is unlike the EVM,
349	    /// which right pads with zeros in this scenario. The return value is the number of bytes
350	    /// written, which allows the caller to detect if this has occurred.
351	    ///
352	    /// [`EXT_CODE_COPY`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3C
353	    fn code(&self, account: Address) -> Vec<u8>;
354	    /// Gets the size of the code in bytes at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
355	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODESIZE`].
356	    ///
357	    /// [`EXT_CODESIZE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3B
358	    fn code_size(&self, account: Address) -> usize;
359	    /// Gets the code hash of the account at the given address. The semantics are equivalent
360	    /// to that of the EVM's [`EXT_CODEHASH`] opcode. Note that the code hash of an account without
361	    /// code will be the empty hash
362	    /// `keccak("") = c5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470`.
363	    ///
364	    /// [`EXT_CODEHASH`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3F
365	    fn code_hash(&self, account: Address) -> B256;
366	}
367	
368	/// Provides the ability to pay for memory growth of a Stylus contract.
369	pub trait MemoryAccess {
370	    /// The `entrypoint!` macro handles importing this hostio, which is required if the
371	    /// program's memory grows. Otherwise compilation through the `ArbWasm` precompile will revert.
372	    /// Internally the Stylus VM forces calls to this hostio whenever new WASM pages are allocated.
373	    /// Calls made voluntarily will unproductively consume gas.
374	    fn pay_for_memory_grow(&self, pages: u16);
375	}
376	
377	/// Provides access to transaction details of a Stylus contract.
378	pub trait MessageAccess {
379	    /// Gets the address of the account that called the program. For normal L2-to-L2 transactions
380	    /// the semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`CALLER`] opcode, including in cases
381	    /// arising from [`DELEGATE_CALL`].
382	    ///
383	    /// For L1-to-L2 retryable ticket transactions, the top-level sender's address will be aliased.
384	    /// See [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`] for more information on how this works.
385	    ///
386	    /// [`CALLER`]: https://www.evm.codes/#33
387	    /// [`DELEGATE_CALL`]: https://www.evm.codes/#f4
388	    /// [`Retryable Ticket Address Aliasing`]: https://developer.arbitrum.io/arbos/l1-to-l2-messaging#address-aliasing
389	    fn msg_sender(&self) -> Address;
390	    /// Whether the current call is reentrant.
391	    fn msg_reentrant(&self) -> bool;
392	    /// Get the ETH value in wei sent to the program. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
393	    /// EVM's [`CALLVALUE`] opcode.
394	    ///
395	    /// [`CALLVALUE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#34
396	    fn msg_value(&self) -> U256;
397	    /// Gets the top-level sender of the transaction. The semantics are equivalent to that of the
398	    /// EVM's [`ORIGIN`] opcode.
399	    ///
400	    /// [`ORIGIN`]: https://www.evm.codes/#32
401	    fn tx_origin(&self) -> Address;
402	}
403	
404	/// Provides access to metering values such as EVM gas and Stylus ink used and remaining,
405	/// as well as details of their prices based on the host environment.
406	pub trait MeteringAccess {
407	    /// Gets the amount of gas left after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics are
408	    /// equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode.
409	    ///
410	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
411	    fn evm_gas_left(&self) -> u64;
412	    /// Gets the amount of ink remaining after paying for the cost of this hostio. The semantics
413	    /// are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS`] opcode, except the units are in ink. See
414	    /// [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on Stylus's compute pricing.
415	    ///
416	    /// [`GAS`]: https://www.evm.codes/#5a
417	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
418	    fn evm_ink_left(&self) -> u64;
419	    /// Gets the gas price in wei per gas, which on Arbitrum chains equals the basefee. The
420	    /// semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's [`GAS_PRICE`] opcode.
421	    ///
422	    /// [`GAS_PRICE`]: https://www.evm.codes/#3A
423	    fn tx_gas_price(&self) -> U256;
424	    /// Gets the price of ink in evm gas basis points. See [`Ink and Gas`] for more information on
425	    /// Stylus's compute-pricing model. Arbitrum enforces a minimum gas price floor, so tx ink
426	    /// price should always return a value greater than zero.
427	    ///
428	    /// [`Ink and Gas`]: https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering
429	    fn tx_ink_price(&self) -> u32;
430	
431	    /// Computes the units of gas per a specified amount of ink.
432	    fn ink_to_gas(&self, ink: u64) -> u64 {
433	        let price = self.tx_ink_price();
434	        if price == 0 {
435	            return 0;
436	        }
437	        ink / price as u64
438	    }
439	
440	    /// Computes the units of ink per a specified amount of gas.
441	    fn gas_to_ink(&self, gas: u64) -> u64 {
442	        gas.saturating_mul(self.tx_ink_price().into())
443	    }
444	}
445	
446	/// Provides access to the ability to emit logs from a Stylus contract.
447	pub trait RawLogAccess {
448	    /// Emits an EVM log with the given number of topics and data, the first bytes of which should
449	    /// be the 32-byte-aligned topic data. The semantics are equivalent to that of the EVM's
450	    /// [`LOG0`], [`LOG1`], [`LOG2`], [`LOG3`], and [`LOG4`] opcodes based on the number of topics
451	    /// specified. Requesting more than `4` topics will induce a revert.
452	    ///
453	    /// [`LOG0`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a0
454	    /// [`LOG1`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a1
455	    /// [`LOG2`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a2
456	    /// [`LOG3`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a3
457	    /// [`LOG4`]: https://www.evm.codes/#a4
458	    fn emit_log(&self, input: &[u8], num_topics: usize);
459	    /// Emits a raw log from topics and data.
460	    fn raw_log(&self, topics: &[B256], data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), &'static str>;
461	}
462	
463	/// Provides access to the ability to emit typed logs from a Stylus contract.
464	pub trait LogAccess: RawLogAccess {
465	    /// Emits a typed alloy log.
466	    ///
467	    /// ```rust,ignore
468	    /// sol! {
469	    ///    event Transfer(
470	    ///        address indexed from,
471	    ///        address indexed to,
472	    ///        uint256 indexed token_id
473	    ///    );
474	    /// }
475	    ///
476	    /// self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, token_id });
477	    /// ```
478	    fn log<T: SolEvent>(&self, event: T) {
479	        // According to the alloy docs, encode_topics_raw fails only if the array is too small
480	
481	        let mut topics = [WordToken::default(); 4];
482	        event.encode_topics_raw(&mut topics).unwrap();
483	
484	        let count = T::TopicList::COUNT;
485	        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(32 * count);
486	        for topic in &topics[..count] {
487	            bytes.extend_from_slice(topic.as_slice());
488	        }
489	        event.encode_data_to(&mut bytes);
490	        self.emit_log(&bytes, count)
491	    }
492	}
493	
494	impl<T: RawLogAccess> LogAccess for T {}

7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11

13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
