15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value

41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.

content.content:
1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).
51

content.content:
1	//! A vesting wallet handles the vesting of Ether and ERC-20 tokens for a given
2	//! beneficiary.
3	//!
4	//! A vesting wallet is an ownable contract that can receive native currency and
5	//! [`crate::token::erc20::Erc20`] tokens, and release these assets to the
6	//! wallet owner, also referred to as "beneficiary", according to a vesting
7	//! schedule.
8	//!
9	//! Any assets transferred to this contract will follow the vesting schedule as
10	//! if they were locked from the beginning. Consequently, if the vesting has
11	//! already started, any amount of tokens sent to this contract will (at least
12	//! partly) be immediately releasable.
13	//!
14	//! By setting the duration to 0, one can configure this contract to behave like
15	//! an asset timelock that hold tokens for a beneficiary until a specified time.
16	//!
17	//! NOTE: Since the wallet is [`Ownable`], and ownership
18	//! can be transferred, it is possible to sell unvested tokens. Preventing this
19	//! in a smart contract is difficult, considering that: 1) a beneficiary address
20	//! could be a counterfactually deployed contract, 2) there is likely to be a
21	//! migration path for EOAs to become contracts in the near future.
22	//!
23	//! NOTE: When using this contract with any token whose balance is adjusted
24	//! automatically (i.e. a rebase token), make sure to account the supply/balance
25	//! adjustment in the vesting schedule to ensure the vested amount is as
26	//! intended.
27	
28	use alloc::{
29	    string::{String, ToString},
30	    vec,
31	    vec::Vec};
32	
33	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, Address, U256, U64};
34	use stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError;
35	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
36	pub use sol::*;
37	use stylus_sdk::{call::{call}, function_selector, prelude::*, storage::{StorageMap, StorageU256, StorageU64}};
38	
39	use crate::{
40	    access::ownable::{self, Ownable},
41	    token::erc20::{
42	        interface::Erc20Interface,
43	        utils::{safe_erc20, ISafeErc20, SafeErc20}},
44	    utils::{introspection::erc165::IErc165, math::storage::AddAssignChecked}};
45	
46	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
47	mod sol {
48	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
49	
50	    sol! {
51	        /// Emitted when `amount` of Ether has been released.
52	        ///
53	        /// * `amount` - Total Ether released.
54	        #[derive(Debug)]
55	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
56	        event EtherReleased(uint256 amount);
57	
58	        /// Emitted when `amount` of ERC-20 `token` has been released.
59	        ///
60	        /// * `token` - Address of the token being released.
61	        /// * `amount` - Number of tokens released.
62	        #[derive(Debug)]
63	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
64	        event ERC20Released(address indexed token, uint256 amount);
65	    }
66	
67	    sol! {
68	        /// Indicates an error related to the underlying Ether transfer.
69	        #[derive(Debug)]
70	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
71	        error ReleaseEtherFailed(string reason);
72	
73	        /// Indicates that a low-level call failed.
74	        #[derive(Debug)]
75	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
76	        error FailedCall();

478	        // SAFETY: total vested amount is by definition greater than or equal to
479	        // the released amount.
480	        self.vested_amount_eth(self.vm().block_timestamp()) - self.released_eth()
481	    }

487	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
488	        let vested = self.vested_amount_erc20(token, self.vm().block_timestamp())?;
489	        // SAFETY: total vested amount is by definition greater than or equal to
490	        // the released amount.
491	        Ok(vested - self.released_erc20(token))
492	    }

495	    fn release_eth(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
496	        let amount = self.releasable_eth();
497	
498	        self.released.add_assign_checked(
499	            amount,
500	            "total released should not exceed `U256::MAX`",
501	        );
502	
503	        let owner = self.ownable.owner();
504	
505	        call(Call::new_in(self).value(amount), owner, &[])?;
506	
507	        self.vm().log(EtherReleased { amount });
508	
509	        Ok(())
510	    }

512	    #[selector(name = "release")]
513	    fn release_erc20(&mut self, token: Address) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
514	        let amount = self.releasable_erc20(token)?;
515	        let owner = self.ownable.owner();
516	
517	        self.erc20_released.setter(token).add_assign_checked(
518	            amount,
519	            "total released should not exceed `U256::MAX`",
520	        );
521	
522	        self.safe_erc20.safe_transfer(token, owner, amount)?;
523	
524	        self.vm().log(ERC20Released { token, amount });
525	
526	        Ok(())
527	    }

530	    fn vested_amount_eth(&self, timestamp: u64) -> U256 {
531	        let total_allocation = self.vm().balance(self.vm().contract_address())
532	            .checked_add(self.released_eth())
533	            .expect("total allocation should not exceed `U256::MAX`");
534	
535	        self.vesting_schedule(total_allocation, U64::from(timestamp))

540	        &mut self,

544	        let erc20 = Erc20Interface::new(token);

547	            .map_err(|_| InvalidToken { token })?;

551	            .expect("total allocation should not exceed `U256::MAX`");
552	
553	        Ok(self.vesting_schedule(total_allocation, U64::from(timestamp)))

557	impl VestingWallet {
558	    /// Virtual implementation of the vesting formula. This returns the amount
559	    /// vested, as a function of time, for an asset given its total
560	    /// historical allocation.
561	    ///
562	    /// # Arguments
563	    ///
564	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
565	    /// * `total_allocation` - Total vested amount.
566	    /// * `timestamp` - Point in time for which to calculate the vested amount.
567	    ///
568	    /// # Panics
569	    ///
570	    /// * If scaled, total allocation (mid calculation) exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
571	    fn vesting_schedule(&self, total_allocation: U256, timestamp: U64) -> U256 {
572	        let timestamp = U256::from(timestamp);
573	
574	        if timestamp < self.start() {
575	            U256::ZERO
576	        } else if timestamp >= self.end() {
577	            total_allocation
578	        } else {
579	            // SAFETY: `timestamp` is guaranteed to be greater than
580	            // `self.start()` as checked by earlier bounds.
581	            let elapsed = timestamp - self.start();
582	
583	            let scaled_allocation = total_allocation
584	                .checked_mul(elapsed)
585	                .expect("scaled allocation exceeds `U256::MAX`");
586	
587	            // SAFETY: `self.duration()` is non-zero. If `self.duration()` were
588	            // zero, then `end == start`, meaning that `timestamp >= self.end()`
589	            // and the function would have returned earlier.
590	            scaled_allocation / self.duration()
591	        }
592	    }
593	}

10	/// An [`Erc721`] token that can be burned (destroyed).
11	#[interface_id]
12	#[public]
13	pub trait IErc721Burnable {
14	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
15	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
16	
17	    /// Burns `token_id`.
18	    /// The approval is cleared when the token is burned.
19	    ///
20	    /// # Arguments
21	    ///
22	    /// * `value` - Amount to be burnt.
23	    ///
24	    /// # Errors
25	    ///
26	    /// * [`erc721::Error::NonexistentToken`] - If token does not exist.
27	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If the caller does not have
28	    ///   the right to approve.
29	    ///
30	    /// # Events
31	    ///
32	    /// * [`erc721::Transfer`].
33	    fn burn(&mut self, token_id: U256) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
34	}
35	
36	#[public]
37	impl IErc721Burnable for Erc721 {
38	    type Error = erc721::Error;
39	
40	    fn burn(&mut self, token_id: U256) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
41	        // Setting an "auth" arguments enables the
42	        // [`super::super::Erc721::_is_authorized`] check which verifies that
43	        // the token exists (from != [`Address::ZERO`]).
44	        //
45	        // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is not 0
46	        // here.
47	        self._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender())?;
48	        Ok(())
49	    }
50	}
51	#[cfg(test)]

67	        contract
68	            .sender(alice)

1	//! Optional `Enumerable` extension of the ERC-721 standard.
2	//!
3	//! This implements an optional extension of [`super::super::Erc721`] defined in
4	//! the EIP that adds enumerability of all the token ids in the contract as well
5	//! as all token ids owned by each account.
6	//!
7	//! CAUTION: [`super::super::Erc721`] extensions that implement custom
8	//! [`super::super::Erc721::balance_of`] logic, such as `Erc721Consecutive`,
9	//! interfere with enumerability and should not be used together with
10	//! [`Erc721Enumerable`].
11	
12	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
13	
14	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, uint, Address, U256};
15	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
16	pub use sol::*;
17	use stylus_sdk::{stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError, prelude::*, storage::{StorageMap, StorageU256, StorageVec}};
18	
19	use crate::{
20	    token::erc721::{self, IErc721},
21	    utils::introspection::erc165::IErc165};
22	
23	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
24	mod sol {
25	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
26	
27	    sol! {
28	        /// Indicates an error when an `owner`'s token query
29	        /// was out of bounds for `index`.
30	        ///
31	        /// NOTE: The owner being [`Address::ZERO`]
32	        /// indicates a global out of bounds index.
33	        #[derive(Debug)]
34	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
35	        error ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex(address owner, uint256 index);
36	
37	        /// Indicates an error related to batch minting not allowed.
38	        #[derive(Debug)]
39	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
40	        error ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint();
41	    }
42	}
43	
44	/// An [`Erc721Enumerable`] extension error.
45	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
46	pub enum Error {
47	    /// Indicates an error when an `owner`'s token query
48	    /// was out of bounds for `index`.
49	    ///
50	    /// NOTE: The owner being [`Address::ZERO`]
51	    /// indicates a global out of bounds index.
52	    OutOfBoundsIndex(ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex),
53	
54	    /// Indicates an error related to batch minting not allowed.
55	    EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint(ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint)}
56	
57	impl MethodError for Error {
58	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
59	        self.into()
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	/// State of an [`Erc721Enumerable`] contract.
64	#[storage]
65	pub struct Erc721Enumerable {
66	    /// Maps owners to a mapping of indices to tokens ids.
67	    pub(crate) owned_tokens: StorageMap<Address, StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>>,
68	    /// Maps tokens ids to indices in `owned_tokens`.
69	    pub(crate) owned_tokens_index: StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>,
70	    /// Stores all tokens ids.
71	    pub(crate) all_tokens: StorageVec<StorageU256>,
72	    /// Maps indices at `all_tokens` to tokens ids.
73	    pub(crate) all_tokens_index: StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>}
74	
75	/// This is the interface of the optional `Enumerable` extension
76	/// of the ERC-721 standard.
77	#[interface_id]
78	#[public]
79	pub trait IErc721Enumerable {
80	    /// The error type associated to this ERC-721 enumerable trait
81	    /// implementation.
82	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
83	
84	    /// Returns a token ID owned by `owner` at a given `index` of its token
85	    /// list.
86	    ///
87	    /// Use along with [`super::super::Erc721::balance_of`] to enumerate all of
88	    /// `owner`'s tokens.
89	    ///
90	    /// # Arguments
91	    ///
92	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
93	    /// * `owner` - Address of token's owner.
94	    /// * `index` - Index of the token at `owner`'s tokens list.
95	    ///
96	    /// # Errors
97	    ///
98	    /// * [`Error::OutOfBoundsIndex`] - If an `owner`'s token query is out of
99	    ///   bounds for `index`.
100	    fn token_of_owner_by_index(
101	        &self,
102	        owner: Address,
103	        index: U256,
104	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
105	
106	    /// Returns the total amount of tokens stored by the contract.
107	    ///
108	    /// # Arguments
109	    ///
110	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
111	    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256;
112	
113	    /// Returns a token ID at a given `index` of all the tokens
114	    /// stored by the contract.
115	    ///
116	    /// Use along with [`Self::total_supply`] to
117	    /// enumerate all tokens.
118	    ///
119	    /// # Arguments
120	    ///
121	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
122	    /// * `index` - Index of the token in all tokens list.
123	    ///
124	    /// # Errors
125	    ///
126	    /// * [`Error::OutOfBoundsIndex`] - If an `owner`'s token query is out of
127	    ///   bounds for `index`.
128	    fn token_by_index(&self, index: U256) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
129	}
130	
131	#[public]
132	#[implements(IErc721Enumerable<Error = Error>, IErc165)]
133	impl Erc721Enumerable {}
134	
135	#[public]
136	impl IErc721Enumerable for Erc721Enumerable {
137	    type Error = Error;
138	
139	    fn token_of_owner_by_index(
140	        &self,
141	        owner: Address,
142	        index: U256,
143	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
144	        let token = self.owned_tokens.getter(owner).get(index);
145	
146	        if token.is_zero() {
147	            Err(ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex { owner, index }.into())
148	        } else {
149	            Ok(token)
150	        }
151	    }
152	
153	    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
154	        let tokens_length = self.all_tokens.len();
155	        U256::from(tokens_length)
156	    }
157	
158	    fn token_by_index(&self, index: U256) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
159	        self.all_tokens.get(index).ok_or(
160	            ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex { owner: Address::ZERO, index }.into(),
161	        )
162	    }
163	}
164	
165	#[public]
166	impl IErc165 for Erc721Enumerable {
167	    fn supports_interface(&self, interface_id: B32) -> bool {
168	        <Self as IErc721Enumerable>::interface_id() == interface_id
169	            || <Self as IErc165>::interface_id() == interface_id
170	    }
171	}
172	
173	impl Erc721Enumerable {
174	    /// Function to add a token to this extension's
175	    /// ownership-tracking data structures.
176	    ///
177	    /// # Arguments
178	    ///
179	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
180	    /// * `to` - Address representing the new owner of the given `token_id`.
181	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be added to the tokens list of the
182	    ///   given address.
183	    /// * `erc721` - Read access to a contract providing [`IErc721`] interface.
184	    ///
185	    /// # Errors
186	    ///
187	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidOwner`] - If owner address is
188	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
189	    pub fn _add_token_to_owner_enumeration(
190	        &mut self,
191	        to: Address,
192	        token_id: U256,
193	        erc721: &impl IErc721<Error = erc721::Error>,
194	    ) -> Result<(), erc721::Error> {
195	        let length = erc721.balance_of(to)? - uint!(1_U256);
196	        self.owned_tokens.setter(to).setter(length).set(token_id);
197	        self.owned_tokens_index.setter(token_id).set(length);
198	
199	        Ok(())
200	    }
201	
202	    /// Function to add a token to this extension's token
203	    /// tracking data structures.
204	    ///
205	    /// # Arguments
206	    ///
207	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
208	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be added to the tokens list.
209	    pub fn _add_token_to_all_tokens_enumeration(&mut self, token_id: U256) {
210	        let index = self.total_supply();
211	
212	        self.all_tokens_index.setter(token_id).set(index);
213	        self.all_tokens.push(token_id);
214	    }
215	
216	    /// Function to remove a token from this extension's
217	    /// ownership-tracking data structures.
218	    ///
219	    /// Note that while the token is not assigned a new owner,
220	    /// the `self.owned_tokens_index` mapping is NOT updated:
221	    /// this allows for  gas optimizations e.g.
222	    /// when performing a transfer operation (avoiding double writes).
223	    ///
224	    /// This has O(1) time complexity, but alters the order
225	    /// of the `self.owned_tokens` array.
226	    ///
227	    /// # Arguments
228	    ///
229	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
230	    /// * `from` - Address representing the previous owner of the given
231	    ///   `token_id`.
232	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be removed from the tokens list of the
233	    ///   given address.
234	    /// * `erc721` - Read access to a contract providing [`IErc721`] interface.
235	    ///
236	    /// # Errors
237	    ///
238	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidOwner`] - If owner address is
239	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
240	    pub fn _remove_token_from_owner_enumeration(
241	        &mut self,
242	        from: Address,
243	        token_id: U256,
244	        erc721: &impl IErc721<Error = erc721::Error>,
245	    ) -> Result<(), erc721::Error> {
246	        // To prevent a gap in from's tokens array,
247	        // we store the last token in the index of the token to delete,
248	        // and then delete the last slot (swap and pop).
249	        let last_token_index = erc721.balance_of(from)?;
250	        let token_index = self.owned_tokens_index.get(token_id);
251	
252	        let mut owned_tokens_by_owner = self.owned_tokens.setter(from);
253	
254	        // When the token to delete is the last token,
255	        // the swap operation is unnecessary.
256	        if token_index != last_token_index {
257	            let last_token_id = owned_tokens_by_owner.get(last_token_index);
258	
259	            // Move the last token to the slot of the to-delete token.
260	            owned_tokens_by_owner.setter(token_index).set(last_token_id);
261	            // Update the moved token's index.
262	            self.owned_tokens_index.setter(last_token_id).set(token_index);
263	        }
264	
265	        // This also deletes the contents at the last position of the array.
266	        self.owned_tokens_index.delete(token_id);
267	        owned_tokens_by_owner.delete(last_token_index);
268	
269	        Ok(())
270	    }
271	
272	    /// Function to remove a token from this extension's
273	    /// token tracking data structures.
274	    ///
275	    /// This has O(1) time complexity,
276	    /// but alters the order of the `self.all_tokens` array.
277	    ///
278	    /// # Arguments
279	    ///
280	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
281	    /// * `token_id` -  ID of the token to be removed from the tokens list.
282	    ///
283	    /// # Panics
284	    ///
285	    /// * The function should not panic in a regular way.
286	    pub fn _remove_token_from_all_tokens_enumeration(
287	        &mut self,
288	        token_id: U256,
289	    ) {
290	        // To prevent a gap in the tokens array,
291	        // we store the last token in the index of the token to delete,
292	        // and then delete the last slot (swap and pop).
293	        let last_token_index = U256::from(self.all_tokens.len() - 1);
294	        let token_index = self.all_tokens_index.get(token_id);
295	
296	        // When the token to delete is the last token,
297	        // the swap operation is unnecessary.
298	        // However, since this occurs so
299	        // rarely (when the last minted token is burnt)
300	        // that we still do the swap here
301	        // to avoid the gas cost of adding an 'if' statement
302	        // (like in `self._remove_token_from_owner_enumeration`).
303	        let last_token_id = self
304	            .all_tokens
305	            .get(last_token_index)
306	            .expect("token at given index must exist");
307	
308	        // Move the last token to the slot of the to-delete token.
309	        self.all_tokens
310	            .setter(token_index)
311	            .expect("slot at given `token_index` must exist")
312	            .set(last_token_id);
313	
314	        // Update the moved token's index.
315	        self.all_tokens_index.setter(last_token_id).set(token_index);
316	
317	        // This also deletes the contents at the last position of the array.
318	        self.all_tokens_index.delete(token_id);
319	        self.all_tokens.pop();
320	    }
321	
322	    /// See [`erc721::Erc721::_increase_balance`].
323	    /// Check if tokens can be minted in batch.
324	    ///
325	    /// Mechanism to be consistent with [Solidity version](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/v5.0.0/contracts/token/ERC721/extensions/ERC721Enumerable.sol#L163-L171)
326	    ///
327	    /// # Arguments
328	    ///
329	    /// * `amount` - The number of tokens to increase balance.
330	    ///
331	    /// # Errors
332	    ///
333	    /// * [`Error::EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint`] - If an `amount` is greater
334	    ///   than `0`.
335	    pub fn _check_increase_balance(amount: u128) -> Result<(), Error> {
336	        if amount > 0 {
337	            Err(ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint {}.into())
338	        } else {
339	            Ok(())
340	        }
341	    }
342	}

1	//! Extension of the ERC-721 token contract to support token wrapping.
2	//!
3	//! Users can deposit and withdraw an "underlying token" and receive a "wrapped
4	//! token" with a matching token ID. This is useful in conjunction with other
5	//! modules.

7	    string::{String, ToString},
8	    vec,
9	    vec::Vec};

43	/// An [`Erc721Wrapper`] error.
44	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
45	pub enum Error {
46	    /// Indicates that an address can't be an owner.
47	    /// For example, [`Address::ZERO`] is a forbidden owner in [`Erc721`].
48	    /// Used in balance queries.
49	    InvalidOwner(erc721::ERC721InvalidOwner),
50	    /// Indicates a `token_id` whose `owner` is the zero address.
51	    NonexistentToken(erc721::ERC721NonexistentToken),
52	    /// Indicates an error related to the ownership over a particular token.
53	    /// Used in transfers.
54	    IncorrectOwner(erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner),
55	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
56	    InvalidSender(erc721::ERC721InvalidSender),
57	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
58	    InvalidReceiver(erc721::ERC721InvalidReceiver),
59	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`, with the reason
60	    /// specified by it.
61	    InvalidReceiverWithReason(erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason),
62	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator`’s approval. Used in transfers.
63	    InsufficientApproval(erc721::ERC721InsufficientApproval),
64	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
65	    /// in approvals.
66	    InvalidApprover(erc721::ERC721InvalidApprover),
67	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator` to be approved. Used in
68	    /// approvals.
69	    InvalidOperator(erc721::ERC721InvalidOperator),
70	    /// The received ERC-721 token couldn't be wrapped.
71	    UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken),
72	    /// An operation with an ERC-721 token failed.
73	    Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation)}
74	
75	impl From<erc721::Error> for Error {
76	    fn from(value: erc721::Error) -> Self {
77	        match value {
78	            erc721::Error::InvalidOwner(e) => Error::InvalidOwner(e),
79	            erc721::Error::NonexistentToken(e) => Error::NonexistentToken(e),
80	            erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(e) => Error::IncorrectOwner(e),
81	            erc721::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
82	            erc721::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
83	            erc721::Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(e) => {
84	                Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(e)
85	            }
86	            erc721::Error::InsufficientApproval(e) => {
87	                Error::InsufficientApproval(e)
88	            }
89	            erc721::Error::InvalidApprover(e) => Error::InvalidApprover(e),
90	            erc721::Error::InvalidOperator(e) => Error::InvalidOperator(e)}
91	    }
92	}

111	/// Interface of an extension of the ERC-721 token contract that supports token
112	/// wrapping.
113	#[interface_id]
114	#[public]
115	pub trait IErc721Wrapper: IErc721Receiver {
116	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
117	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
118	
119	    /// Allow a user to deposit underlying tokens and mint the corresponding
120	    /// `token_ids`.
121	    ///
122	    /// # Arguments
123	    ///
124	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
125	    /// * `account` - The account to deposit tokens to.
126	    /// * `token_ids` - List of underlying token ids to deposit.
127	    ///
128	    /// # Errors
129	    ///
130	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not an
131	    ///   ERC-721 contract.
132	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If an error occurs during
133	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721::transfer_from`] operation on the underlying token.
134	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
135	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
136	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
137	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
138	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
139	    fn deposit_for(
140	        &mut self,
141	        account: Address,
142	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
143	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
144	
145	    /// Allow a user to burn wrapped tokens and withdraw the corresponding
146	    /// `token_ids` of the underlying tokens.
147	    ///
148	    /// # Arguments
149	    ///
150	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
151	    /// * `account` - The account to withdraw tokens to.
152	    /// * `token_ids` - List of underlying token ids to withdraw.
153	    ///
154	    /// # Errors
155	    ///
156	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not an
157	    ///   ERC-721 contract.
158	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If an error occurs during
159	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`] operation on the underlying
160	    ///   token.
161	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist and `auth`
162	    ///   is not [`Address::ZERO`].
163	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If `auth` is not [`Address::ZERO`]
164	    ///   and `auth` does not have a right to approve this token.
165	    fn withdraw_to(
166	        &mut self,
167	        account: Address,
168	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
169	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
170	
171	    /// Returns the underlying token.
172	    ///
173	    /// # Arguments
174	    ///
175	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
176	    #[must_use]
177	    fn underlying(&self) -> Address;
178	}

180	impl Erc721Wrapper {
181	    /// Constructor.
182	    ///
183	    /// # Arguments
184	    ///
185	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
186	    /// * `underlying_token` - The wrapped token.
187	    pub fn constructor(&mut self, underlying_token: Address) {
188	        self.underlying.set(underlying_token);
189	    }
190	
191	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::deposit_for()`] for more information.
192	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
193	    pub fn deposit_for(
194	        &mut self,
195	        account: Address,
196	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
197	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
198	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
199	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
200	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
201	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
202	
203	        for token_id in token_ids {
204	            // This is an "unsafe" transfer that doesn't call any hook on
205	            // the receiver. With [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] being trusted
206	            // (by design of this contract) and no other contracts expected to
207	            // be called from there, we are safe.
208	            match underlying.transfer_from(
209	                Call::new_in(self),
210	                sender,
211	                contract_address,
212	                token_id,
213	            ) {
214	                Ok(()) => (),
215	                Err(e) => {
216	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
217	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
218	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
219	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
220	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
221	                                        .to_string()},
222	                            ));
223	                        }
224	                    }
225	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
226	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
227	                    ));
228	                }
229	            }
230	
231	            erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
232	        }
233	
234	        Ok(true)
235	    }
236	
237	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::withdraw_to()`] for more information.
238	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
239	    pub fn withdraw_to(
240	        &mut self,
241	        account: Address,
242	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
243	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
244	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
245	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
246	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
247	
248	        for token_id in token_ids {
249	            // Setting the `auth` argument enables the `_is_authorized` check
250	            // which verifies that the token exists (from != 0).
251	            // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is
252	            // not 0 here.
253	            erc721._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, sender)?;
254	            match underlying.safe_transfer_from(
255	                Call::new_in(self),
256	                self.vm().contract_address(),
257	                account,
258	                token_id,
259	                vec![].into(),
260	            ) {
261	                Ok(()) => (),
262	                Err(e) => {
263	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
264	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
265	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
266	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
267	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
268	                                        .to_string()},
269	                            ));
270	                        }
271	                    }
272	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
273	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
274	                    ));
275	                }
276	            }
277	        }
278	
279	        Ok(true)
280	    }
281	
282	    /// Allow minting on direct ERC-721 transfers to this contract.
283	    ///
284	    /// # Arguments
285	    ///
286	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
287	    /// * `operator` - The operator of the transfer.
288	    /// * `from` - The sender of the transfer.
289	    /// * `token_id` - The token id of the transfer.
290	    /// * `data` - The data of the transfer.
291	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
292	    ///
293	    /// # Errors
294	    ///
295	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `self.vm().msg_sender()` is not the underlying
296	    ///   token.
297	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
298	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
299	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
300	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
301	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
302	    pub fn on_erc721_received(
303	        &mut self,
304	        _operator: Address,
305	        from: Address,
306	        token_id: U256,
307	        _data: &Bytes,
308	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
309	    ) -> Result<B32, Error> {
310	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
311	        if self.underlying() != sender {
312	            return Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken {
313	                token: sender}));
314	        }
315	
316	        erc721._safe_mint(from, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
317	
318	        Ok(RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR)
319	    }
320	
321	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] for more information.
322	    #[must_use]
323	    pub fn underlying(&self) -> Address {
324	        self.underlying.get()
325	    }
326	
327	    /// Mints wrapped tokens to cover any underlying tokens that would have been
328	    /// function that can be exposed with access control if desired.
329	    ///
330	    /// # Arguments
331	    ///
332	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
333	    /// * `account` - The account to mint tokens to.
334	    /// * `token_id` - A mutable reference to the Erc20 contract.
335	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
336	    ///
337	    /// # Errors
338	    ///
339	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not a
340	    ///   [`Erc721`] contract, or the contract fails to execute the call.
341	    /// * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`] - If the underlying token is not owned by
342	    ///   the contract.
343	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
344	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
345	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
346	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
347	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
348	    fn _recover(
349	        &mut self,
350	        account: Address,
351	        token_id: U256,
352	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
353	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
354	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
355	
356	        let owner = underlying.owner_of(Call::new_in(self), token_id).map_err(
357	            |_| {
358	                Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
359	                    token: self.underlying()})
360	            },
361	        )?;
362	
363	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
364	        if owner != contract_address {
365	            return Err(erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(
366	                erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner {
367	                    sender: contract_address,
368	                    token_id,
369	                    owner},
370	            )
371	            .into());
372	        }
373	
374	        erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
375	
376	        Ok(token_id)
377	    }
378	}

#!/usr/bin/perl
# Rewrites SDK 0.9 import paths to their SDK 0.10 locations.
# Usage: perl fix_sdk_imports.pl FILE...
use strict;
use warnings;

my %drop = map { $_ => 1 } qw(msg evm block contract);

for my $file (@ARGV) {
    open my $fh, '<', $file or die "open $file: $!";
    local $/;
    my $src = <$fh>;
    close $fh;
    my $orig = $src;

    # Standalone `use stylus_sdk::msg;` style lines for removed globals.
    $src =~ s/^[ \t]*use stylus_sdk::(?:msg|evm|block|contract);\n//mg;

    # Grouped imports: drop removed globals from `use stylus_sdk::{...};`.
    $src =~ s{use stylus_sdk::\{(.*?)\};}{
        my $group = $1;
        my @keep;
        for my $item (split /,/, $group) {
            (my $t = $item) =~ s/^\s+|\s+$//g;
            next if $t eq '';
            next if $drop{$t};
            push @keep, $t;
        }
        @keep ? "use stylus_sdk::{" . join(', ', @keep) . "};" : "";
    }gse;

    # Path renames for the SDK 0.10 call module.
    $src =~ s/\bstylus_sdk::call::MethodError\b/stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError/g;
    $src =~ s/\bstylus_sdk::call::Call\b/stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::Call/g;
    $src =~ s/\bstylus_sdk::call::Error\b/stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error/g;
    $src =~ s/\bstylus_sdk::call::StaticCallContext\b/stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::StaticCallContext/g;
    $src =~ s/\bcall::MethodError\b/stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError/g;
    $src =~ s/\bcall::Call\b/stylus_core::calls::Call/g;
    $src =~ s/\bcall::Error\b/stylus_core::calls::errors::Error/g;
    $src =~ s/\bcall::StaticCallContext\b/stylus_core::calls::StaticCallContext/g;

    if ($src ne $orig) {
        open my $out, '>', $file or die "write $file: $!";
        print $out $src;
        close $out;
        print "updated $file\n";
    }
}

144	/// An [`Erc721`] error defined as described in [ERC-6093].
145	///
146	/// [ERC-6093]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6093
147	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
148	pub enum Error {
149	    /// Indicates that an address can't be an owner.
150	    /// For example, [`Address::ZERO`] is a forbidden owner in [`Erc721`].
151	    /// Used in balance queries.
152	    InvalidOwner(ERC721InvalidOwner),
153	    /// Indicates a `token_id` whose `owner` is the zero address.
154	    NonexistentToken(ERC721NonexistentToken),
155	    /// Indicates an error related to the ownership over a particular token.
156	    /// Used in transfers.
157	    IncorrectOwner(ERC721IncorrectOwner),
158	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
159	    InvalidSender(ERC721InvalidSender),
160	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
161	    InvalidReceiver(ERC721InvalidReceiver),
162	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`, with the reason
163	    /// specified by it.
164	    InvalidReceiverWithReason(InvalidReceiverWithReason),
165	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator`’s approval. Used in transfers.
166	    InsufficientApproval(ERC721InsufficientApproval),
167	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
168	    /// in approvals.
169	    InvalidApprover(ERC721InvalidApprover),
170	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator` to be approved. Used in
171	    /// approvals.
172	    InvalidOperator(ERC721InvalidOperator)}

203	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;

211	    ///
212	    /// # Errors

215	    fn balance_of(&self, owner: Address) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;

218	    ///
219	    /// # Arguments
220	    ///

222	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
223	    ///
224	    /// # Errors
225	    ///
226	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist.
227	    fn owner_of(&self, token_id: U256) -> Result<Address, Self::Error>;
228	
229	    /// Safely transfers `token_id` token from `from` to `to`, checking first
230	    /// that contract recipients are aware of the [`Erc721`] protocol to
231	    /// prevent tokens from being forever locked.
232	    ///
233	    /// # Arguments
234	    ///
235	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
236	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
237	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
238	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
239	    ///
240	    /// # Errors
241	    ///
242	    /// * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`]  - If the previous owner is not `from`.
243	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If the caller does not have the
244	    ///   right to approve.
245	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist.
246	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
247	    ///   [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
248	    /// interface id or returned with error, `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
249	    ///
250	    /// # Events
251	    ///
252	    /// * [`Transfer`].
253	    fn safe_transfer_from(
254	        &mut self,
255	        from: Address,
256	        to: Address,
257	        token_id: U256,
258	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
259	
260	    /// Safely transfers `token_id` token from `from` to `to`.
261	    ///
262	    /// # Arguments
263	    ///
264	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
265	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
266	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
267	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
268	    /// * `data` - Additional data with no specified format, sent in the call to

270	    ///
271	    /// # Errors
272	    ///
273	    ///  * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`] - If the previous owner is not `from`.
274	    ///  * [`Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If the caller does not have the

276	    ///  * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist.
277	    ///  * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
278	    ///    [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its interface
279	    ///    id or returned with error, or `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
280	    ///
281	    /// # Events
282	    ///
283	    /// * [`Transfer`].
284	    #[selector(name = "safeTransferFrom")]
285	    fn safe_transfer_from_with_data(
286	        &mut self,
287	        from: Address,
288	        to: Address,
289	        token_id: U256,
290	        data: Bytes,
291	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;

293	    /// Transfers `token_id` token from `from` to `to`.
294	    ///

353	    /// Approve or remove `operator` as an operator for the caller.

402	#[public]
403	#[implements(IErc721<Error = Error>, IErc165)]
404	impl Erc721 {}
405	
406	#[public]
407	impl IErc721 for Erc721 {
408	    type Error = Error;
409	
410	    fn balance_of(&self, owner: Address) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
411	        if owner.is_zero() {
412	            return Err(ERC721InvalidOwner { owner: Address::ZERO }.into());
413	        }
414	        Ok(self.balances.get(owner))
415	    }
416	
417	    fn owner_of(&self, token_id: U256) -> Result<Address, Self::Error> {
418	        self._require_owned(token_id)
419	    }
420	
421	    fn safe_transfer_from(
422	        &mut self,
423	        from: Address,
424	        to: Address,
425	        token_id: U256,
426	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
427	        self.safe_transfer_from_with_data(from, to, token_id, vec![].into())
428	    }
429	
430	    #[selector(name = "safeTransferFrom")]
431	    fn safe_transfer_from_with_data(
432	        &mut self,
433	        from: Address,
434	        to: Address,
435	        token_id: U256,
436	        data: Bytes,
437	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
438	        self.transfer_from(from, to, token_id)?;
439	        self._check_on_erc721_received(self.vm().msg_sender(), from, to, token_id, &data)
440	    }
441	
442	    fn transfer_from(
443	        &mut self,
444	        from: Address,
445	        to: Address,
446	        token_id: U256,
447	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
448	        if to.is_zero() {
449	            return Err(
450	                ERC721InvalidReceiver { receiver: Address::ZERO }.into()
451	            );
452	        }
453	
454	        // Setting an "auth" argument enables the `_is_authorized` check which
455	        // verifies that the token exists (`from != 0`). Therefore, it is
456	        // not needed to verify that the return value is not 0 here.
457	        let previous_owner = self._update(to, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender())?;
458	        if previous_owner != from {
459	            return Err(ERC721IncorrectOwner {
460	                sender: from,
461	                token_id,
462	                owner: previous_owner}
463	            .into());
464	        }
465	        Ok(())
466	    }
467	
468	    fn approve(
469	        &mut self,
470	        to: Address,
471	        token_id: U256,
472	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
473	        self._approve(to, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender(), true)
474	    }
475	
476	    fn set_approval_for_all(
477	        &mut self,

869	    /// function will check that `auth` is either the owner of the token, or
870	    /// approved to operate on all tokens held by this owner.
871	    ///
872	    /// # Arguments
873	    ///
874	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
875	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
876	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
877	    /// * `auth` - Account used for authorization of the update.
878	    /// * `emit_event` - Emit an [`Approval`] event flag.
879	    ///
880	    /// # Errors
881	    ///
882	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist.
883	    /// * [`Error::InvalidApprover`] - If `auth` does not have a right to
884	    ///   approve this token.
885	    ///
886	    /// # Events
887	    ///
888	    /// * [`Approval`].
889	    pub fn _approve(
890	        &mut self,
891	        to: Address,
892	        token_id: U256,
893	        auth: Address,
894	        emit_event: bool,
895	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
896	        // Avoid reading the owner unless necessary.
897	        if emit_event || !auth.is_zero() {
898	            let owner = self._require_owned(token_id)?;
899	
900	            // We do not use [`Self::_is_authorized`] because single-token
901	            // approvals should not be able to call `approve`.
902	            if !auth.is_zero()
903	                && owner != auth
904	                && !self.is_approved_for_all(owner, auth)
905	            {
906	                return Err(ERC721InvalidApprover { approver: auth }.into());
907	            }
908	
909	            if emit_event {
910	                self.vm().log(Approval { owner, approved: to, token_id });
911	            }
912	        }
913	
914	        self.token_approvals.setter(token_id).set(to);
915	        Ok(())
916	    }
917	
918	    /// Approve `operator` to operate on all of `owner`'s tokens.
919	    ///
920	    /// # Arguments
921	    ///
922	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
923	    /// * `owner` - Account the token's owner.
924	    /// * `operator` - Account to add to the set of authorized operators.
925	    /// * `approved` - Whether permission will be granted. If true, this means.
926	    ///
927	    /// # Errors
928	    ///
929	    /// * [`Error::InvalidOperator`] - If `operator` is [`Address::ZERO`].
930	    ///
931	    /// # Events
932	    ///
933	    /// * [`ApprovalForAll`].
934	    pub fn _set_approval_for_all(
935	        &mut self,
936	        owner: Address,
937	        operator: Address,
938	        approved: bool,
939	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
940	        if operator.is_zero() {
941	            return Err(ERC721InvalidOperator { operator }.into());
942	        }
943	
944	        self.operator_approvals.setter(owner).setter(operator).set(approved);
945	        self.vm().log(ApprovalForAll { owner, operator, approved });
946	        Ok(())
947	    }
948	
949	    /// Reverts if the `token_id` doesn't have a current owner (it hasn't been
950	    /// minted, or it has been burned). Returns the owner.
951	    ///
952	    /// Overrides to ownership logic should be done to
953	    /// [`Self::_owner_of`].
954	    ///
955	    /// # Arguments
956	    ///
957	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
958	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
959	    ///
960	    /// # Errors
961	    ///
962	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If token does not exist.
963	    pub fn _require_owned(&self, token_id: U256) -> Result<Address, Error> {
964	        let owner = self._owner_of(token_id);
965	        if owner.is_zero() {
966	            return Err(ERC721NonexistentToken { token_id }.into());
967	        }
968	        Ok(owner)
969	    }
970	
971	    /// Performs an acceptance check for the provided `operator` by calling
972	    /// [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] on the `to` address. The
973	    /// `operator` is generally the address that initiated the token transfer
974	    /// (i.e. `self.vm().msg_sender()`).
975	    ///
976	    /// The acceptance call is not executed and treated as a no-op if the
977	    /// target address doesn't contain code (i.e. an EOA). Otherwise, the
978	    /// recipient must implement [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] and
979	    /// return the acceptance magic value to accept the transfer.
980	    ///
981	    /// # Arguments
982	    ///
983	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
984	    /// * `operator` - Account to add to the set of authorized operators.
985	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
986	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
987	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
988	    /// * `data` - Additional data with no specified format, sent in call to
989	    ///   `to`.
990	    ///
991	    /// # Errors
992	    ///
993	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
994	    ///   [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its interface
995	    ///   id or returned an error.
996	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If
997	    ///   [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] reverted with revert data.
998	    pub fn _check_on_erc721_received(
999	        &mut self,
1000	        operator: Address,
1001	        from: Address,
1002	        to: Address,
1003	        token_id: U256,
1004	        data: &Bytes,
1005	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
1006	        if !to.has_code() {
1007	            return Ok(());
1008	        }
1009	
1010	        let receiver = IErc721ReceiverInterface::new(to);
1011	        let call = Call::new_in(self);
1012	        let result = receiver.on_erc_721_received(
1013	            call,
1014	            operator,
1015	            from,
1016	            token_id,
1017	            data.to_vec().into(),
1018	        );
1019	
1020	        let id = match result {
1021	            Ok(id) => id,
1022	            Err(e) => {
1023	                if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
1024	                    if !reason.is_empty() {
1025	                        return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
1026	                            InvalidReceiverWithReason {
1027	                                reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
1028	                                    .to_string()},
1029	                        ));
1030	                    }
1031	                }
1032	
1033	                // Non-IERC721Receiver implementer.
1034	                return Err(ERC721InvalidReceiver { receiver: to }.into());
1035	            }
1036	        };
1037	
1038	        // Token rejected.
1039	        if id != RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR {
1040	            return Err(ERC721InvalidReceiver { receiver: to }.into());
1041	        }
1042	
1043	        Ok(())
1044	    }
1045	}

content.content:
"examples/eddsa",
]
exclude = ["fuzz", "templates/crypto-erc20"]

# Explicitly set the resolver to version 2, which is the default for packages
# with edition >= 2021.
# https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2021/default-cargo-resolver.html
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
authors = ["OpenZeppelin"]
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus"
version = "0.3.0"

[workspace.lints.rust]
missing_docs = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2021_compatibility = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(coverage_nightly)'] }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
all = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Stylus SDK related
stylus-sdk = "=0.10.10"
# Devnet tooling used by the end-to-end tests and benches (dev-only).
stylus-tools = { version = "=0.10.10", features = ["integration-tests"] }

# `alloy` is used by the end-to-end tests and benches. The contracts only depend
# on `alloy-primitives` and `alloy-sol-types`, which must match the versions the
# Stylus SDK is built against.
alloy = { version = "=1.7.3", features = ["essentials", "signer-local"] }
alloy-primitives = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false, features = [
  "tiny-keccak",
] }
alloy-sol-types = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }
alloy-sol-macro = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }

ruint = "^1.17.1"

eyre = "0.6.8"
keccak-const = "0.2.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
regex = "1.10.4"
tiny-keccak = { version = "2.0.2", features = ["keccak"] }
tokio = { version = "1.45", features = ["full"] }
futures = "0.3.30"
num-traits = "0.2.14"
zeroize = { version = "1.8.1", features = ["derive"] }
proptest = "1"
educe = "0.6.0"
hex-literal = "0.4.1"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
static_assertions = "1.1.0"

# procedural macros
syn = { version = "2.0.58", features = ["full"] }
proc-macro2 = "1.0.79"
quote = "1.0.35"

# members
e2e = { path = "lib/e2e" }
e2e-proc = { path = "lib/e2e-proc" }
openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "contracts" }
openzeppelin-stylus-proc = { path = "contracts-proc", version = "=0.3.0" }
openzeppelin-crypto = { path = "lib/crypto" }

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
opt-level = "z"
strip = true
lto = true
debug = false
rpath = false
debug-assertions = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[workspace.metadata.typos]
default = { extend-ignore-identifiers-re = [
  # ignore hex data samples.
  "[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]",
] }
files = { extend-exclude = [] }

1	//! Permit Contract.
2	//!
3	//! Extension of the ERC-20 standard allowing approvals to be made
4	//! via signatures, as defined in the [ERC].
5	//!
6	//! Adds the `permit` method, which can be used to change an account’s
7	//! ERC20 allowance (see [`crate::token::erc20::IErc20::allowance`])
8	//! by presenting a message signed by the account.
9	//! By not relying on [`erc20::IErc20::approve`],
10	//! the token holder account doesn’t need to send a transaction,
11	//! and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
12	//!
13	//! [ERC]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612
14	
15	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
16	
17	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, keccak256, Address, B256, U256, U8};

20

22	    token::erc20::{self, Erc20},
23	    utils::{
24	        cryptography::eip712::IEip712,
25	        nonces::{INonces, Nonces},
26	        precompiles::{
27	            primitives::ecrecover::{
28	                self, ECDSAInvalidSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignatureS},

225	        r: B256,

2	//! in [ERC-2309].

4	//! This extension allows the minting large batches of tokens, during
5	//! contract construction only. For upgradeable contracts, this implies that
6	//! batch minting is only available during proxy deployment, and not in
7	//! subsequent upgrades. These batches are limited to 5000 tokens at a time by
8	//! default to accommodate off-chain indexers.

1	//! Implementation of the ERC-3156 Flash loans extension, as defined in
2	//! [ERC-3156].
3	//!
4	//! Adds the [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`] method, which provides flash
5	//! loan support at the token level. By default there is no fee, but this can be
6	//! changed by overriding [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`].
7	//!
8	//! NOTE: When this extension is used along with the
9	//! [`crate::token::erc20::extensions::Capped`] extension,
10	//! [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`] will not correctly reflect the
11	//! maximum that can be flash minted. We recommend overriding
12	//! [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`] so that it correctly reflects the
13	//! supply cap.
14	//!
15	//! [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
16	
17	// TODO: once ERC20Votes is implemented, include it in the comment above next to
18	// ERC20Capped.

63	/// An [`Erc20FlashMint`] extension error.
64	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
65	pub enum Error {
66	    /// Indicate that the loan token is not supported or valid.
67	    UnsupportedToken(ERC3156UnsupportedToken),
68	    /// Indicate an error related to the loan value exceeding the maximum.
69	    ExceededMaxLoan(ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan),
70	    /// Indicate that the receiver of a flashloan is not a valid
71	    /// [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] implementer.
72	    ERC3156InvalidReceiver(ERC3156InvalidReceiver),
73	    /// Indicates an error related to the current balance of `sender`. Used in
74	    /// transfers.
75	    InsufficientBalance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientBalance),
76	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
77	    InvalidSender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSender),
78	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
79	    InvalidReceiver(erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver),
80	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
81	    /// transfers.
82	    InsufficientAllowance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientAllowance),
83	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
84	    /// approvals.
85	    InvalidSpender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSpender),
86	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
87	    /// in approvals. approver Address initiating an approval operation.
88	    InvalidApprover(erc20::ERC20InvalidApprover)}
89	
90	impl From<erc20::Error> for Error {
91	    fn from(value: erc20::Error) -> Self {
92	        match value {
93	            erc20::Error::InsufficientBalance(e) => {
94	                Error::InsufficientBalance(e)
95	            }
96	            erc20::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
97	            erc20::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
98	            erc20::Error::InsufficientAllowance(e) => {
99	                Error::InsufficientAllowance(e)
100	            }
101	            erc20::Error::InvalidSpender(e) => Error::InvalidSpender(e),
102	            erc20::Error::InvalidApprover(e) => Error::InvalidApprover(e)}
103	    }
104	}

166	/// Interface of the ERC-3156 Flash Lender, as defined in [ERC-3156].
167	///
168	/// [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
169	#[interface_id]
170	#[public]
171	pub trait IErc3156FlashLender {
172	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
173	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
174	
175	    /// Returns the maximum amount of tokens available for loan.
176	    ///
177	    /// NOTE: This function does not consider any form of supply cap, so in case
178	    /// it's used in a token with a cap like
179	    /// [`crate::token::erc20::extensions::Capped`], make sure to override this
180	    /// function to integrate the cap instead of [`U256::MAX`].
181	    ///
182	    /// # Arguments
183	    ///
184	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
185	    /// * `token` - The address of the token that is requested.
186	    #[must_use]
187	    fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address) -> U256;
188	
189	    /// Returns the fee applied when doing flash loans.
190	    ///
191	    /// # Arguments
192	    ///
193	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
194	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned.
195	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
196	    ///
197	    /// # Errors
198	    ///
199	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If the token is not supported.
200	    ///
201	    /// # Examples
202	    ///
203	    /// ```rust,ignore
204	    /// fn flash_fee(&self, token: Address, value: U256) -> Result<U256, flash_mint::Error> {
205	    ///     self.erc20_flash_mint.flash_fee(token, value)
206	    /// }
207	    /// ```
208	    fn flash_fee(
209	        &self,
210	        token: Address,
211	        value: U256,
212	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
213	
214	    /// Performs a flash loan.
215	    ///
216	    /// New tokens are minted and sent to the `receiver`, who is required to
217	    /// implement the [`IERC3156FlashBorrower`] interface. By the end of the
218	    /// flash loan, the receiver is expected to own value + fee tokens and have
219	    /// them approved back to the token contract itself so they can be burned.
220	    ///
221	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
222	    ///
223	    /// # Arguments
224	    ///
225	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
226	    /// * `receiver` - The receiver of the flash loan. Should implement the
227	    ///   [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] interface.
228	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned. Only [`self.vm().contract_address()`]
229	    ///   is supported.
230	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
231	    /// * `data` - Arbitrary data that is passed to the receiver.
232	    ///
233	    /// # Errors
234	    ///
235	    /// * [`Error::ExceededMaxLoan`] - If the `value` is greater than the value
236	    ///   returned by [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
237	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `token` is not supported.
238	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `token` address is not a contract
239	    ///   , the contract fails to execute the call, or the receiver does not
240	    ///   return [`BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE`].
241	    ///
242	    /// # Events
243	    ///
244	    /// * [`erc20::Transfer`].
245	    /// * [`erc20::Approval`].
246	    ///
247	    /// # Panics
248	    ///
249	    /// * If the new (temporary) total supply exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
250	    /// * If the sum of the loan value and fee exceeds the maximum value of
251	    ///   [`U256::MAX`].
252	    fn flash_loan(
253	        &mut self,
254	        receiver: Address,
255	        token: Address,
256	        value: U256,
257	        data: Bytes,
258	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
259	}
260	
261	impl Erc20FlashMint {
262	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
263	    #[must_use]
264	    pub fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address, erc20: &erc20::Erc20) -> U256 {
265	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
266	            U256::MAX - erc20.total_supply()
267	        } else {
268	            U256::MIN
269	        }
270	    }
271	
272	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_fee`].
273	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
274	    pub fn flash_fee(
275	        &self,
276	        token: Address,
277	        _value: U256,
278	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
279	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
280	            Ok(self.flash_fee_value.get())
281	        } else {
282	            Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC3156UnsupportedToken { token }))
283	        }
284	    }
285	
286	    // This function can reenter, but it doesn't pose a risk because it always
287	    // preserves the property that the amount minted at the beginning is always
288	    // recovered and burned at the end, or else the entire function will revert.
289	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`].
290	    #[allow(clippy::missing_panics_doc, clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
291	    pub fn flash_loan(
292	        &mut self,
293	        receiver: Address,
294	        token: Address,
295	        value: U256,
296	        data: &Bytes,
297	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
298	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
299	        let max_loan = self.max_flash_loan(token, erc20);
300	        if value > max_loan {
301	            return Err(Error::ExceededMaxLoan(ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan {
302	                max_loan}));
303	        }
304	
305	        let fee = self.flash_fee(token, value)?;
306	        if !Address::has_code(&receiver) {
307	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
308	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
309	            ));
310	        }
311	        erc20._mint(receiver, value)?;
312	        let loan_receiver = IERC3156FlashBorrower::new(receiver);
313	        let loan_return = loan_receiver
314	            .on_flash_loan(
315	                Call::new_in(self),
316	                self.vm().msg_sender(),
317	                token,
318	                value,
319	                fee,
320	                data.to_vec().into(),
321	            )
322	            .map_err(|_| {
323	                Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(ERC3156InvalidReceiver {
324	                    receiver})
325	            })?;
326	        if loan_return != BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE {
327	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
328	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
329	            ));
330	        }
331	
332	        let allowance = value
333	            .checked_add(fee)
334	            .expect("allowance should not exceed `U256::MAX`");
335	        erc20._spend_allowance(receiver, self.vm().contract_address(), allowance)?;
336	
337	        let flash_fee_receiver = self.flash_fee_receiver_address.get();
338	
339	        if fee.is_zero() || flash_fee_receiver.is_zero() {
340	            erc20._burn(receiver, allowance)?;
341	        } else {
342	            erc20._burn(receiver, value)?;
343	            erc20._transfer(receiver, flash_fee_receiver, fee)?;
344	        }
345	
346	        Ok(true)
347	    }
348	}

1	//! Wrappers around ERC-20 operations that throw on failure (when the token
2	//! contract returns false).
3	//!
4	//! Tokens that return no value (and instead revert or
5	//! throw on failure) are also supported, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
6	//! successful.
7	//!
8	//! To use this library, you can add a `#[implements(ISafeErc20<Error =
9	//! Error>)]` attribute to your contract, which allows you to call the safe
10	//! operations as `contract.safe_transfer(token_addr, ...)`, etc.
11	
12	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
13	use stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError;
14	
15	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, Address, U256};
16	use alloy_sol_types::{sol_data::Bool, SolCall, SolType};
17	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
18	pub use sol::*;
19	use stylus_sdk::{abi::Bytes, call::RawCall, function_selector, prelude::*};
20	
21	use crate::{
22	    token::erc20::interface::Erc20Interface,
23	    utils::introspection::erc165::IErc165};
24	
25	const BOOL_TYPE_SIZE: usize = 32;
26	
27	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
28	mod sol {
29	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
30	
31	    sol! {
32	        /// An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.
33	        ///
34	        /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token.
35	        #[derive(Debug)]
36	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
37	        error SafeErc20FailedOperation(address token);
38	
39	        /// Indicates a failed [`ISafeErc20::safe_decrease_allowance`] request.
40	        ///
41	        /// * `spender` - Address of future tokens' spender.
42	        /// * `current_allowance` - Current allowance of the `spender`.
43	        /// * `requested_decrease` - Requested decrease in allowance for `spender`.
44	        #[derive(Debug)]
45	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
46	        error SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance(
47	            address spender,
48	            uint256 current_allowance,
49	            uint256 requested_decrease
50	        );
51	    }
52	}
53	
54	/// A [`SafeErc20`] error.
55	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
56	pub enum Error {
57	    /// An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.
58	    SafeErc20FailedOperation(SafeErc20FailedOperation),
59	    /// Indicates a failed [`ISafeErc20::safe_decrease_allowance`] request.
60	    SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance(SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance)}
61	
62	impl MethodError for Error {
63	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
64	        self.into()
65	    }
66	}
67	
68	use token::{Erc1363Interface, IERC20};
69	
70	mod token {
71	    #![allow(missing_docs)]
72	    #![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
73	
74	    use alloc::vec;
75	
76	    alloy_sol_types::sol! {
77	        /// Interface of the ERC-20 token.
78	        interface IERC20 {
79	            function allowance(address owner, address spender) external view returns (uint256);
80	            function approve(address spender, uint256 value) external returns (bool);
81	            function transfer(address to, uint256 value) external returns (bool);
82	            function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 value) external returns (bool);
83	        }
84	    }
85	
86	    stylus_sdk::prelude::sol_interface! {
87	        interface Erc1363Interface {
88	            function transferAndCall(address to, uint256 value, bytes calldata data) external returns (bool);
89	            function transferFromAndCall(address from, address to, uint256 value, bytes calldata data) external returns (bool);
90	            function approveAndCall(address spender, uint256 value, bytes calldata data) external returns (bool);
91	        }
92	    }
93	}

95	/// State of a [`SafeErc20`] Contract.
96	#[storage]
97	pub struct SafeErc20;
98	
99	/// NOTE: Implementation of [`TopLevelStorage`] to be able use `&mut self` when
100	/// calling other contracts and not `&mut (impl TopLevelStorage +
101	/// BorrowMut<Self>)`. Should be fixed in the future by the Stylus team.
102	unsafe impl TopLevelStorage for SafeErc20 {}
103	
104	/// Required interface of a [`SafeErc20`] utility contract.
105	#[interface_id]
106	#[public]
107	pub trait ISafeErc20 {
108	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
109	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
110	
111	    /// Transfer `value` amount of `token` from the calling contract to `to`. If
112	    /// `token` returns no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
113	    /// successful.
114	    ///
115	    /// # Arguments
116	    ///
117	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
118	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
119	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
120	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
121	    ///
122	    /// # Errors
123	    ///
124	    ///  * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
125	    ///    contract , the contract fails to execute the call or the call returns
126	    ///    value that is not `true`.
127	    fn safe_transfer(
128	        &mut self,
129	        token: Address,
130	        to: Address,
131	        value: U256,
132	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
133	
134	    /// Transfer `value` amount of `token` from `from` to `to`, spending the
135	    /// approval given by `from` to the calling contract. If `token` returns
136	    /// no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be successful.
137	    ///
138	    /// # Arguments
139	    ///
140	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
141	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
142	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
143	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
144	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
145	    ///
146	    /// # Errors
147	    ///
148	    ///  * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
149	    ///    contract , the contract fails to execute the call or the call returns
150	    ///    value that is not `true`.
151	    fn safe_transfer_from(
152	        &mut self,
153	        token: Address,
154	        from: Address,
155	        to: Address,
156	        value: U256,
157	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
158	
159	    /// Variant of [`Self::safe_transfer`] that returns a `bool` instead of
160	    /// reverting if the operation is not successful.
161	    ///
162	    /// # Arguments
163	    ///
164	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
165	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
166	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
167	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
168	    fn try_safe_transfer(
169	        &mut self,
170	        token: Address,
171	        to: Address,
172	        value: U256,
173	    ) -> bool;
174	
175	    /// Variant of [`Self::safe_transfer_from`] that returns a `bool` instead of
176	    /// reverting if the operation is not successful.
177	    ///
178	    /// # Arguments
179	    ///
180	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
181	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
182	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
183	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
184	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
185	    fn try_safe_transfer_from(
186	        &mut self,
187	        token: Address,
188	        from: Address,
189	        to: Address,
190	        value: U256,
191	    ) -> bool;
192	
193	    /// Increase the calling contract's allowance toward `spender` by `value`.
194	    /// If `token` returns no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
195	    /// successful.
196	    ///
197	    /// # Arguments
198	    ///
199	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
200	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
201	    /// * `spender` - Account that will spend the tokens.
202	    /// * `value` - Value to increase current allowance for `spender`.
203	    ///
204	    /// # Errors

206	    /// * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
