content.content:
1	# E2E porting brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Context: the OpenZeppelin Stylus library moved to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust 1.91.0. The
4	contracts crate (`contracts/`) is migrated and compiles on the `bench` branch, which is
5	your base commit. Each example under `examples/` has a contract (`src/lib.rs`), an
6	`export-abi` binary (`src/main.rs`) and end-to-end tests (`tests/`, gated by the `e2e`
7	feature). The old end-to-end framework (`lib/e2e`, `lib/e2e-proc`) is being removed. Its
8	replacement is the `devnet` crate (`lib/devnet`), a thin layer over the SDK devnet
9	(`stylus-tools`, a pinned Nitro node in Docker).
10	
11	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on the `bench` commit. Read these before
12	editing:
13	- `lib/devnet/src/lib.rs` and `lib/devnet/src/assert.rs`: the helpers you will use.
14	- `/tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md`: the API decisions (SDK 0.10 accessors, call contexts, `Self::Error`).
15	- `/tmp/bench/notes/agent-brief.md`: the general rules (no global accessors, `#[public]` tags,
16	  commit trailer, no commented-out code, keep every scenario).
17	
18	## What you own
19	Only the directories listed in your task: the example crates (`src/`, `tests/`, `Cargo.toml`,
20	`abi/` if present) and nothing else. If you need a change elsewhere (workspace `Cargo.toml`,
21	`lib/devnet`, `contracts/`), do not make it; list it under "requests" in your report.
22	
23	## Source migration (contract code in `examples/*/src/`)
24	- Apply the API map: host access through `self.vm()`, `Call::new()` / `Call::new_mutating(self)`
25	  bound to a local before `self.vm()` is borrowed, concrete error types in `#[public]` impls
26	  (`Result<_, Self::Error>` fails under `export-abi`: write the concrete type), no
27	  `stylus_sdk::{evm,msg,block,contract}`, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error,MethodError}`.
28	- Keep the ABI, selectors, error types and behaviour exactly as they are.
29	- `main.rs` (export-abi binary) keeps working: `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`.
30	
31	## End-to-end test migration (`examples/*/tests/`)
32	Keep the file gating `#![cfg(feature = "e2e")]` and the crate's `e2e = []` feature.
33	
34	Replace the old helpers as follows:
35	
36	| v0.3.0 (`e2e`)                              | new (`devnet`)                                            |
37	|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
38	| `#[e2e::test] async fn t(alice: Account) -> Result<()>` | `#[tokio::test] async fn t() -> eyre::Result<()> { let alice = devnet::funded_account().await?; ... }` (add more accounts with `devnet::funded_account()`; each account gets 10 ETH) |
39	| `alice.as_deployer().with_constructor(ctr).deploy().await?.contract_address` | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), Some((arg1, arg2, ...).abi_encode_params().into())).await?` (`use alloy::sol_types::SolValue`) |
40	| `alice.as_deployer().deploy().await?.contract_address` (no constructor) | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), None).await?` |
41	| `constructor!(...)` / `default_ctr()` helpers | the tuple of constructor args, ABI-encoded as above (keep the helper function names if they still read well) |
42	| `alice.wallet` (typed contract handle)      | `Contract::new(addr, alice.provider().await?)` (the sol! bindings in `tests/abi/mod.rs` stay as they are if they compile) |
43	| `send!(x)`                                  | `x.send().await` |
44	| `watch!(x)`                                 | `x.send().await?.watch().await?` |
45	| `receipt!(x)`                               | `x.send().await?.get_receipt().await?` |
46	| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `alloy::contract::Error` | `devnet::assert::reverted_with(&err, &E { .. })` |
47	| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `eyre::Report` (deployment) | `devnet::assert::deployment_reverted_with(&report, &E { .. })` |
48	| `x.panicked_with(code)` (`Panic`)           | `devnet::assert::is_execution_revert(&err)` (the same strength as v0.3.0; do not claim a panic code you cannot see) |
49	| `receipt.emits(E { .. })` (`EventExt`)      | `devnet::assert::emits(&receipt, &E { .. })` |
50	| `ContractInitializationError` marker        | the `deployment_reverted_with` check above |
51	
52	Rules:
53	1. Every scenario and every assertion survives, success and failure. Do not delete, weaken
54	   or merge a test. If an old assertion is weaker than what the chain now reports, you may
55	   strengthen it; say so in the report.
56	2. Each test uses its own accounts (`devnet::funded_account()`), so tests can run in parallel.
57	3. Test names stay the same (the test inventory is compared name by name).
58	4. No commented-out code, no `#[ignore]` added. If v0.3.0 had an `#[ignore]` on a test, keep it
59	   and say why in the report.
60	5. `devnet::wasm_path(name)` takes the crate name (`erc20-example`), not the file name.
61	
62	## Building and running
63	- Build the contract WASM for your examples (release, stable toolchain):
64	    cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <crate> [-p <crate> ...]
65	  (run this from your worktree; the files land in `<worktree>/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/`).
66	  `devnet::wasm_path` uses `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` if set, otherwise the workspace `target/`
67	  next to the `lib/devnet` crate, so it finds the files in your worktree.
68	- Run the end-to-end tests against the shared devnet, serialized with the other agents:
69	    RPC_URL=http://localhost:55000 lockf /tmp/bench/e2e.lock cargo test -p <crate> --features e2e
70	  `lockf` serializes the runs, because all agents fund accounts from the same devnet owner key.
71	  Do not start a devnet yourself and do not change the RPC URL. If the devnet is down, say so
72	  in your report and continue with the compile checks.
73	- Compile checks: `cargo check -p <crate> --features e2e --tests` and
74	  `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`, and the wasm build above.
75	- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --features e2e -- -D warnings` (fix warnings in your files).
76	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>`.
77	
78	## Git
79	- Commit on your branch in small logical commits. Each message ends with only this trailer:
80	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
81	  Do not add any other Co-Authored-By line. Do not push. Do not switch branches.
82	
83	## Final report (at most 40 lines)
84	- Crates changed and commits (`git log --oneline <base>..HEAD`).
85	- Test inventory per crate: count of `#[e2e::test]` before and `#[tokio::test]` after, and the names
86	  that differ (there should be none).
87	- Verification: which of the compile checks, wasm build, clippy and E2E runs passed, with the
88	  number of tests passed/failed/ignored per crate. Paste the failing test names and the first
89	  error line for each failure. Do not claim a pass you did not see.
90	- Requests for other owners and blockers.

description: Reading /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md

content.content:
1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).
51

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.

content.content:
# E2E porting brief (read fully before editing)

Context: the OpenZeppelin Stylus library moved to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust 1.91.0. The
contracts crate (`contracts/`) is migrated and compiles on the `bench` branch, which is
your base commit. Each example under `examples/` has a contract (`src/lib.rs`), an
`export-abi` binary (`src/main.rs`) and end-to-end tests (`tests/`, gated by the `e2e`
feature). The old end-to-end framework (`lib/e2e`, `lib/e2e-proc`) is being removed. Its
replacement is the `devnet` crate (`lib/devnet`), a thin layer over the SDK devnet
(`stylus-tools`, a pinned Nitro node in Docker).

Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on the `bench` commit. Read these before
editing:
- `lib/devnet/src/lib.rs` and `lib/devnet/src/assert.rs`: the helpers you will use.
- `/tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md`: the API decisions (SDK 0.10 accessors, call contexts, `Self::Error`).
- `/tmp/bench/notes/agent-brief.md`: the general rules (no global accessors, `#[public]` tags,
  commit trailer, no commented-out code, keep every scenario).

## What you own
Only the directories listed in your task: the example crates (`src/`, `tests/`, `Cargo.toml`,
`abi/` if present) and nothing else. If you need a change elsewhere (workspace `Cargo.toml`,
`lib/devnet`, `contracts/`), do not make it; list it under "requests" in your report.

## Source migration (contract code in `examples/*/src/`)
- Apply the API map: host access through `self.vm()`, `Call::new()` / `Call::new_mutating(self)`
  bound to a local before `self.vm()` is borrowed, concrete error types in `#[public]` impls
  (`Result<_, Self::Error>` fails under `export-abi`: write the concrete type), no
  `stylus_sdk::{evm,msg,block,contract}`, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error,MethodError}`.
- Keep the ABI, selectors, error types and behaviour exactly as they are.
- `main.rs` (export-abi binary) keeps working: `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`.

## End-to-end test migration (`examples/*/tests/`)
Keep the file gating `#![cfg(feature = "e2e")]` and the crate's `e2e = []` feature.

Replace the old helpers as follows:

| v0.3.0 (`e2e`)                              | new (`devnet`)                                            |
|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `#[e2e::test] async fn t(alice: Account) -> Result<()>` | `#[tokio::test] async fn t() -> eyre::Result<()> { let alice = devnet::funded_account().await?; ... }` (add more accounts with `devnet::funded_account()`; each account gets 10 ETH) |
| `alice.as_deployer().with_constructor(ctr).deploy().await?.contract_address` | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), Some((arg1, arg2, ...).abi_encode_params().into())).await?` (`use alloy::sol_types::SolValue`) |
| `alice.as_deployer().deploy().await?.contract_address` (no constructor) | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), None).await?` |
| `constructor!(...)` / `default_ctr()` helpers | the tuple of constructor args, ABI-encoded as above (keep the helper function names if they still read well) |
| `alice.wallet` (typed contract handle)      | `Contract::new(addr, alice.provider().await?)` (the sol! bindings in `tests/abi/mod.rs` stay as they are if they compile) |
| `send!(x)`                                  | `x.send().await` |
| `watch!(x)`                                 | `x.send().await?.watch().await?` |
| `receipt!(x)`                               | `x.send().await?.get_receipt().await?` |
| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `alloy::contract::Error` | `devnet::assert::reverted_with(&err, &E { .. })` |
| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `eyre::Report` (deployment) | `devnet::assert::deployment_reverted_with(&report, &E { .. })` |
| `x.panicked_with(code)` (`Panic`)           | `devnet::assert::is_execution_revert(&err)` (the same strength as v0.3.0; do not claim a panic code you cannot see) |
| `receipt.emits(E { .. })` (`EventExt`)      | `devnet::assert::emits(&receipt, &E { .. })` |
| `ContractInitializationError` marker        | the `deployment_reverted_with` check above |

Rules:
1. Every scenario and every assertion survives, success and failure. Do not delete, weaken
   or merge a test. If an old assertion is weaker than what the chain now reports, you may
   strengthen it; say so in the report.
2. Each test uses its own accounts (`devnet::funded_account()`), so tests can run in parallel.
3. Test names stay the same (the test inventory is compared name by name).
4. No commented-out code, no `#[ignore]` added. If v0.3.0 had an `#[ignore]` on a test, keep it
   and say why in the report.
5. `devnet::wasm_path(name)` takes the crate name (`erc20-example`), not the file name.

## Building and running
- Build the contract WASM for your examples (release, stable toolchain):
    cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <crate> [-p <crate> ...]
  (run this from your worktree; the files land in `<worktree>/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/`).
  `devnet::wasm_path` uses `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` if set, otherwise the workspace `target/`
  next to the `lib/devnet` crate, so it finds the files in your worktree.
- Run the end-to-end tests against the shared devnet, serialized with the other agents:
    RPC_URL=http://localhost:55000 lockf /tmp/bench/e2e.lock cargo test -p <crate> --features e2e
  `lockf` serializes the runs, because all agents fund accounts from the same devnet owner key.
  Do not start a devnet yourself and do not change the RPC URL. If the devnet is down, say so
  in your report and continue with the compile checks.
- Compile checks: `cargo check -p <crate> --features e2e --tests` and
  `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`, and the wasm build above.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --features e2e -- -D warnings` (fix warnings in your files).
- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>`.

## Git
- Commit on your branch in small logical commits. Each message ends with only this trailer:
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Do not add any other Co-Authored-By line. Do not push. Do not switch branches.

## Final report (at most 40 lines)

# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
Import paths:
  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())

Traits:
  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }

Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

------
# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)

Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.

Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.

Read first:
- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).

## Ownership
Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).

## What "done" means for your files
1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
     let vm = TestVM::default();
     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
   may change (documented in the report).
7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.

## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
- Check your files only:
    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1

  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.

[workspace.package]

[workspace.lints.rust]
missing_docs = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2021_compatibility = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Stylus SDK related
stylus-sdk = "=0.10.10"
# Devnet tooling used by the end-to-end tests and benches (dev-only).
stylus-tools = { version = "=0.10.10", features = ["integration-tests"] }

# on `alloy-primitives` and `alloy-sol-types`, which must match the versions the
# Stylus SDK is built against.

alloy-primitives = { version = "=1.6.0", default-features = false, features = [
  "tiny-keccak",
] }
alloy-sol-types = { version = "=1.6.0", default-features = false }
alloy-sol-macro = { version = "=1.6.0", default-features = false }

ruint = "^1.17.1"

eyre = "0.6.8"
keccak-const = "0.2.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
regex = "1.10.4"
tiny-keccak = { version = "2.0.2", features = ["keccak"] }
tokio = { version = "1.45", features = ["full"] }
futures = "0.3.30"
num-traits = "0.2.14"
zeroize = { version = "1.8.1", features = ["derive"] }
proptest = "1"
educe = "0.6.0"
hex-literal = "0.4.1"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
static_assertions = "1.1.0"

# procedural macros
syn = { version = "2.0.58", features = ["full"] }
proc-macro2 = "1.0.79"
quote = "1.0.35"

# members
e2e = { path = "lib/e2e" }
e2e-proc = { path = "lib/e2e-proc" }
openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "contracts" }
openzeppelin-stylus-proc = { path = "contracts-proc", version = "=0.3.0" }
openzeppelin-crypto = { path = "lib/crypto" }
devnet = { path = "lib/devnet" }

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
opt-level = "z"
strip = true
lto = true
debug = false
rpath = false
debug-assertions = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[workspace.metadata.typos]
default = { extend-ignore-identifiers-re = [
  # ignore hex data samples.
  "[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]",
] }
files = { extend-exclude = [] }

//! Starts a Stylus SDK devnet and keeps it running until Ctrl-C.
//!
//! Run `cargo run -p devnet --bin devnet`, then export the printed `RPC_URL`
//! before running end-to-end tests or benches. Requires Docker.

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> eyre::Result<()> {
    let node = stylus_tools::devnet::Node::new().await?;
    println!("RPC_URL={}", node.rpc());
    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;
    Ok(())
}

# Security review brief (read fully before starting)

Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).

Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.

## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
   are real issues in the code.
7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.

## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
  495-504).
- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
    underlying token's).
  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.

## Test-harness facts you need
- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
  before the call that needs it.
- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).

## How to work
- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
  them in your notes file.
- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
  report (the upgrade guide needs it).

## Commit rules
- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.

## Output
Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).

Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

content.content:
1	# Security review brief (read fully before starting)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
4	1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
5	clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).
6	
7	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
8	Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
9	`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
10	`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.
11	
12	## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
13	1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
14	2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
15	3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
16	4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
17	5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
18	   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
19	6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
20	   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
21	   are real issues in the code.
22	7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.
23	
24	## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
25	Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
26	you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
27	- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
28	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
29	- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
30	  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
31	  495-504).
32	- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
33	- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
34	  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
35	- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
36	  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
37	- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
39	  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
40	- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
41	  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
42	  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
44	  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
45	    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
46	    underlying token's).
47	  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
48	    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
49	    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
50	  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.
51	
52	## Test-harness facts you need
53	- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.
58	- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
59	  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
60	- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
61	- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
62	  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).
63	
64	## How to work
65	- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
66	  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
67	  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
68	  them in your notes file.
69	- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
70	  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
71	  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
72	  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
73	  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
74	- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
75	  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
76	  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
77	  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
78	- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
79	  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
80	- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
81	  report (the upgrade guide needs it).
82	
83	## Commit rules
84	- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
85	- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
86	- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.
87	
88	## Output
89	Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
90	- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
91	- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
92	- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
93	Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
94	held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).
95	
96	Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
97	the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

5	clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).
6	
7	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
8	Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
9	`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
10	`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.
11	
12	## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
13	1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
14	2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
15	3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
16	4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
17	5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
18	   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
19	6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
20	   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
21	   are real issues in the code.
22	7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.
23	
24	## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
25	Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
26	you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
27	- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
28	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
29	- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
30	  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
31	  495-504).
32	- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
33	- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
34	  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
35	- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
36	  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
37	- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
39	  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
40	- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
41	  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
42	  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
44	  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
45	    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
46	    underlying token's).
47	  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
48	    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
49	    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
50	  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.
51	
52	## Test-harness facts you need
53	- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.
58	- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
59	  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
60	- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
61	- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
62	  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).
63	
64	## How to work
65	- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
66	  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
67	  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
68	  them in your notes file.
69	- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
70	  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
71	  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
72	  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
73	  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
74	- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
75	  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
76	  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
77	  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
78	- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
79	  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
80	- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
81	  report (the upgrade guide needs it).
82	
83	## Commit rules
84	- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
85	- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
86	- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.
87	
88	## Output
89	Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
90	- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
91	- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
92	- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
93	Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
94	held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).
95	
96	Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
97	the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

printf '[workspace]\n\n[workspace.networks]\n' > Stylus.toml && cat > scripts/devnet.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Starts or stops the Stylus SDK devnet (a pinned Nitro node in Docker) used by the
# end-to-end tests and the benches.
#
#   scripts/devnet.sh start   builds the devnet binary, starts a node in the background
#                             and prints its RPC URL once it is ready.
#   scripts/devnet.sh stop    stops the node that `start` launched.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
STATE="$ROOT/target/devnet"
mkdir -p "$STATE"

case "${1:-}" in
  start)
    cargo build -p devnet --bin devnet --quiet
    "$ROOT/target/debug/devnet" > "$STATE/devnet.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$STATE/devnet.pid"
    until grep -q 'RPC_URL=' "$STATE/devnet.log"; do
      if ! kill -0 "$(cat "$STATE/devnet.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "the devnet exited, see $STATE/devnet.log" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      sleep 2
    done
    grep -o 'RPC_URL=.*' "$STATE/devnet.log" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-
    ;;
  stop)
    if [ -f "$STATE/devnet.pid" ]; then
      kill -INT "$(cat "$STATE/devnet.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
      rm -f "$STATE/devnet.pid"
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 start|stop" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
EOF
cat > scripts/e2e-tests.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Runs the end-to-end tests of the examples against a Stylus SDK devnet.
#
# One devnet serves the whole run: set RPC_URL to reuse a running node, otherwise a
# devnet is started here and stopped at the end. Extra arguments are passed to
# `cargo test`, for example `scripts/e2e-tests.sh -p erc20-example`.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

291	    /// Reverts if `context.vm().msg_value()` is not
292	    /// [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]. It can be used to avoid
293	    /// `context.vm().msg_value()` stuck in the contract if an upgrade does not
294	    /// perform an initialization call.
295	    ///
296	    /// # Arguments
297	    ///
298	    /// * `context` - Read access to the contract's state.
299	    ///
300	    /// # Errors
301	    ///
302	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If `context.vm().msg_value()` is not
303	    ///   [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`].
304	    fn check_non_payable(
305	        context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>,
306	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
307	        if context.vm().msg_value().is_zero() {
308	            Ok(())
309	        } else {
310	            Err(ERC1967NonPayable {}.into())
311	        }
312	    }

314	    /// Stores a new address in the ERC-1967 implementation slot.
315	    ///
316	    /// # Arguments
317	    ///
318	    /// * `context` - Write access to the contract's state.
319	    /// * `new_implementation` - The new implementation address.
320	    ///
321	    /// # Errors
322	    ///
323	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the `new_implementation` address
324	    ///   is not a valid implementation.
325	    fn set_implementation(
326	        context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>,
327	        new_implementation: Address,
328	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
329	        if !AddressUtils::has_code(context, new_implementation) {
330	            return Err(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
331	                implementation: new_implementation,
332	            }
333	            .into());
334	        }
335	
336	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageAddress>(context, IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT)
337	            .set(new_implementation);
338	
339	        Ok(())
340	    }

342	    /// Stores a new address in the ERC-1967 admin slot.
343	    ///
344	    /// # Arguments
345	    ///
346	    /// * `context` - Write access to the contract's state.
347	    /// * `new_admin` - The new admin address.
348	    ///
349	    /// # Errors
350	    ///
351	    /// * [`Error::InvalidAdmin`] - If the `new_admin` address is not a valid
352	    ///   admin.
353	    fn set_admin(
354	        context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>,
355	        new_admin: Address,
356	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
357	        if new_admin.is_zero() {
358	            return Err(ERC1967InvalidAdmin { admin: new_admin }.into());
359	        }
360	
361	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageAddress>(context, ADMIN_SLOT)
362	            .set(new_admin);
363	
364	        Ok(())
365	    }

367	    /// Stores a new beacon in the ERC-1967 beacon slot.
368	    ///
369	    /// # Arguments
370	    ///
371	    /// * `context` - Mutable access to the contract's state.
372	    /// * `new_beacon` - The new beacon address.
373	    ///
374	    /// # Errors
375	    ///
376	    /// * [`Error::InvalidBeacon`] - If the `new_beacon` address is not a valid
377	    ///   beacon.
378	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the beacon implementation is not
379	    ///   a valid implementation.
380	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the call to the beacon implementation
381	    ///   fails.
382	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the call to the beacon
383	    ///   implementation fails with a revert reason.
384	    fn set_beacon<T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>>(
385	        context: &mut T,
386	        new_beacon: Address,
387	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
388	        if !AddressUtils::has_code(context, new_beacon) {
389	            return Err(ERC1967InvalidBeacon { beacon: new_beacon }.into());
390	        }
391	
392	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageAddress>(context, BEACON_SLOT)
393	            .set(new_beacon);
394	
395	        let beacon_implementation =
396	            Erc1967Utils::get_beacon_implementation(context, new_beacon)?;
397	
398	        if !AddressUtils::has_code(context, beacon_implementation) {
399	            return Err(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
400	                implementation: beacon_implementation,
401	            }
402	            .into());
403	        }
404	
405	        Ok(())
406	    }
407	}

# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
Import paths:
  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())

Traits:
  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }

Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).

56	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
57	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`]) execution
58	/// contexts.
59	///
60	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
61	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
62	///
63	/// Behavior:
64	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
65	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`]), `logic_flag == false` (i.e.,
66	///   the proxy’s storage does not contain this implementation-only flag).
67	///
68	/// Security notes:
69	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
70	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
71	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
72	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
73	        .finalize();
74	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
75	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
76	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
77	
78	    B256::new(slot)
79	};

246	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
247	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
248	///
249	/// # Overview
250	///
251	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
252	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
253	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
254	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
255	///
256	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
257	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
258	/// upgrade flow.
259	///
260	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
261	///
262	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
263	///
264	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
265	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
266	/// slot:
267	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
268	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
269	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
270	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
271	///
272	/// ## Initialization Pattern
273	///
274	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
275	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
276	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
277	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
278	///   `only_proxy()`.
279	///
280	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
281	///
282	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
283	///
284	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
285	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
286	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
287	///    the proxy.
288	///
289	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
290	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
291	/// unauthorized upgrades.
292	///
293	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
294	///
295	/// ## Common Mistakes
296	///
297	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
298	///   number constant does not increase.
299	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
300	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
301	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
302	///
303	/// ## Security Considerations
304	///
305	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
306	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
307	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
308	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
309	///
310	/// # Usage
311	///
312	/// ```rust
313	/// extern crate alloc;
314	///
315	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
316	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
317	///
318	/// #[storage]
319	/// #[entrypoint]
320	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
321	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
322	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
323	///
324	///     // Your contract's state variables
325	///     value: StorageU256,
326	///     // ...
327	/// }
328	///
329	/// #[public]
330	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
331	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
332	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
333	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
334	///     }
335	///
336	///     // Your contract's functions
337	/// }
338	/// ```
339	///
340	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
341	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
342	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
343	#[storage]
344	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
345	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
346	    pub version: StorageU32,
347	}
348	
349	#[public]
350	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
351	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
352	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
353	    ///
354	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
355	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
356	    ///
357	    /// # Arguments
358	    ///
359	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
360	    #[constructor]
361	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
362	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
363	    }
364	
365	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
366	    /// (initializer-like).
367	    ///
368	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
369	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
370	    ///
371	    /// # Arguments
372	    ///
373	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
374	    ///
375	    /// # Errors
376	    ///
377	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
378	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
379	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
380	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
381	    ///
382	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
383	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
384	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
385	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
386	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
387	            ));
388	        }
389	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
390	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
391	                current_version: self.version.get().to(),
392	            }));
393	        }
394	
395	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
396	        Ok(())
397	    }
398	}

406	    #[payable]
407	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
408	        &mut self,
409	        new_implementation: Address,
410	        data: Bytes,
411	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
412	        self.only_proxy()?;
413	        self._upgrade_to_and_call_uups(new_implementation, &data)?;

417	        AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
418	            self,
419	            new_implementation,
420	            &data_set_version,
421	        )?;
422	
423	        Ok(())
424	    }
425	}

427	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
428	    /// Get the logic contract version.
429	    ///
430	    /// # Arguments
431	    ///
432	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
433	    #[must_use]
434	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
435	        VERSION_NUMBER
436	    }
437	
438	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
439	    ///
440	    /// # Arguments
441	    ///
442	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
443	    #[must_use]
444	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
445	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(self, LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
446	    }
447	
448	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
449	    ///
450	    /// # Arguments
451	    ///
452	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
453	    #[must_use]
454	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
455	        self.logic_flag().get()
456	    }
457	
458	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
459	    ///
460	    /// Checks:
461	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`] (checked via
462	    ///    `!self.is_logic()`).
463	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
464	    ///    non-zero).
465	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
466	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
467	    ///
468	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
469	    ///
470	    /// # Security Implications
471	    ///
472	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
473	    /// implementation contract.
474	    ///
475	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
476	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
477	    ///
478	    /// # Edge Cases
479	    ///
480	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
481	    ///   check
482	    ///
483	    /// # Arguments
484	    ///
485	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
486	    ///
487	    /// # Errors
488	    ///
489	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
490	    ///   not met
491	    ///
492	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
493	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
494	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
495	        if self.is_logic()
496	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation(self) == Address::ZERO
497	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
498	        {
499	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
500	        } else {
501	            Ok(())
502	        }
503	    }
504	
505	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
506	    /// [`delegate_call`].
507	    ///
508	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
509	    /// but not through proxies.
510	    ///
511	    /// # Arguments
512	    ///
513	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
514	    ///
515	    /// # Errors
516	    ///
517	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
518	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
519	    ///
520	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
521	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
522	        if self.is_logic() {
523	            Ok(())
524	        } else {
525	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
526	        }
527	    }
528	}

538	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
539	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
540	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
541	    ///
542	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
543	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
544	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
545	    ///
546	    /// # Arguments
547	    ///
548	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
549	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
550	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
551	    ///
552	    /// # Errors
553	    ///
554	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
555	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
556	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
557	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
558	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
559	    ///   not designed to handle it.
560	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
561	    ///   address.
562	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`] to the new
563	    ///   implementation fails.
564	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
565	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
566	    ///
567	    /// # Events
568	    ///
569	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the implementation
570	    ///   is upgraded.
571	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
572	        &mut self,
573	        new_implementation: Address,
574	        data: &Bytes,
575	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
576	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
577	            .proxiable_uuid(self.vm(), Call::new())
578	            .map_err(|_e| {
579	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
580	                    implementation: new_implementation,
581	                })
582	            })?;
583	
584	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
585	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
586	                .map_err(Error::from)
587	        } else {
588	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
589	                slot,
590	            }))
591	        }
592	    }
593	}
